stem: Which description best fits a project in PRINCE2?
option_A: A temporary organization established to deliver business products under an agreed business case
option_B: An ongoing department that maintains business operations
option_C: A permanently funded group for routine service delivery
option_D: Any activity completed by a single specialist
correct_text: A temporary organization established to deliver business products under an agreed business case
why: Projects are temporary and exist to create defined products and change; business-as-usual operations continue after the project.

stem: Which feature normally distinguishes a project from business as usual?
option_A: It has a temporary existence and delivers change
option_B: It has no uncertainty because its outcome is defined
option_C: It never involves people from different functions
option_D: It continues indefinitely once its products are delivered
correct_text: It has a temporary existence and delivers change
why: PRINCE2 describes projects as change-oriented, temporary, cross-functional, unique and uncertain.

stem: Which is one of the five integrated PRINCE2 elements?
why: The integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and project context.

stem: A project uses fixed phases for infrastructure and short iterations for software. What delivery approach is this?
why: Hybrid delivery combines linear-sequential and iterative-incremental approaches.

stem: Which item is NOT one of the seven aspects of project performance managed in PRINCE2?
why: The seven aspects are benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk.

stem: Why do projects usually involve more uncertainty than routine operations?
option_A: They involve unique change, temporary relationships and unfamiliar circumstances
option_B: They are always longer than routine operations
option_C: They can never be planned in stages
option_D: Project boards prohibit lessons from earlier work
correct_text: They involve unique change, temporary relationships and unfamiliar circumstances
why: Project uniqueness, cross-functional work and change create threats and opportunities beyond normal operations.

stem: Which is the purpose of project management?
option_A: To coordinate and control the work needed to achieve agreed project objectives
option_B: To remove the need for business justification
option_C: To replace every specialist delivery method
option_D: To turn temporary projects into permanent departments
correct_text: To coordinate and control the work needed to achieve agreed project objectives
why: Project management plans, delegates, monitors and controls work so agreed objectives can be achieved.

stem: What is the best description of the project context element?
option_A: The circumstances that influence how PRINCE2 is applied to this particular project
option_B: The complete list of tasks for a work package
option_D: A set of requirements that never changes
correct_text: The circumstances that influence how PRINCE2 is applied to this particular project
why: The project context makes the method fit the organizational, commercial, delivery, sustainability and scale conditions.

stem: A project is no longer expected to generate enough value. Which principle points toward stopping it?
why: Investment must remain justified throughout the project, not merely at authorization.

stem: What should a team do with lessons from a previous similar project?
option_A: Review and apply relevant lessons from the start and throughout delivery
option_B: File them only after its own project closes
option_C: Use them only after an exception occurs
option_D: Ignore them because each project is unique
correct_text: Review and apply relevant lessons from the start and throughout delivery
why: Learning is active and continuous: seek, record, apply and share relevant experience.

stem: Which three interests must be represented in project management arrangements?
why: The defined roles and relationships principle ensures the business, users and suppliers are represented.

stem: The project board authorizes work a stage at a time. Which principle is illustrated?
why: Stage boundaries create control points for reviewing progress and authorizing further investment.

stem: A project manager can make decisions within agreed tolerances without requesting board approval each time. Which principle is this?
why: Tolerances define delegated authority; forecast breaches trigger escalation.

stem: Why identify required products and quality expectations before planning detailed activities?
option_A: To apply the focus on products principle
option_C: To replace stage controls with informal updates
option_D: To guarantee benefits on the day of delivery
correct_text: To apply the focus on products principle
why: Product descriptions provide clarity about what must be delivered and the quality it must meet.

stem: How should PRINCE2 be used on a small, low-risk project?
option_A: Apply all principles but scale management arrangements to suit the project
option_B: Remove any principles that feel excessive
option_C: Use identical documentation as a very large programme
option_D: Exclude management of issues and risks entirely
correct_text: Apply all principles but scale management arrangements to suit the project
why: Tailoring adapts the method to circumstances; the seven principles still apply.

stem: A stage is forecast to exceed its cost tolerance. What does manage by exception require?
option_A: Escalate the forecast breach to the next management level
option_B: Wait until the money is actually spent
option_D: Keep the forecast out of board reports
correct_text: Escalate the forecast breach to the next management level
why: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond a delegated tolerance, requiring escalation.

stem: Which statement about PRINCE2 principles is correct?
option_A: All seven apply, although their implementation may be tailored
option_B: A project board may drop a principle in the initiation stage
option_C: They are optional if the project uses agile delivery
option_D: They only apply to the closing process
correct_text: All seven apply, although their implementation may be tailored
why: Principles are the obligations that make a project genuinely PRINCE2-managed.

stem: Who is responsible for recommending tailoring, subject to project board approval?
why: The project manager recommends tailoring; the project board remains accountable for approving it, and decisions are captured in the PID.

stem: Which pair of actions best demonstrates manage by stages?
option_A: Prepare detailed plans for the current stage and seek approval for the next
option_B: Authorize every activity at project outset and avoid reviews
option_C: Deliver all work in one uncontrolled period
option_D: Permit each supplier to redefine project benefits
correct_text: Prepare detailed plans for the current stage and seek approval for the next
why: Manage by stages enables detailed near-term control and board decisions at stage boundaries.

stem: An agreed product description is used to settle a dispute about what the team must deliver. Which principle is most directly supported?
why: An agreed product description anchors expectations around the deliverable instead of just the activities.

stem:
Which TWO statements about tailoring are correct?
1. Terminology may be adapted to organizational usage.
2. The seven principles may be omitted.
3. Control detail may be scaled to project complexity.
4. Risk management may be ignored altogether.
why: Tailoring permits proportionate methods and familiar terminology, not omission of the principles.

stem: A project manager consults users and suppliers when clarifying decision rights. Which principle is central?
why: Clear authority must be paired with effective working relationships across all three stakeholder interests.

stem: Identify the missing term: Limits of delegated authority are expressed through agreed [?].
why: Tolerances establish when a management level can act independently and when it must escalate.

stem: Why should the business case be revisited as a project progresses?
option_A: Changes in costs, risks and expected value may affect justification
option_B: The original estimate is always inaccurate
option_C: PRINCE2 requires a new business sponsor at each stage
option_D: The project manager must avoid all product changes
correct_text: Changes in costs, risks and expected value may affect justification
why: Continued justification requires ongoing evidence that the project remains desirable, viable and achievable.

stem: Who counts as a stakeholder in PRINCE2?
option_A: Anyone who can affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves affected by the project
option_B: Only people on the project board
option_C: Only people employed by the commissioning business
option_D: Only users who sign the acceptance form
correct_text: Anyone who can affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves affected by the project
why: Stakeholders extend beyond the formal project management team and include affected people and groups.

stem: What does change management primarily concern?
option_A: Moving an organization from its current way of operating to a target state
option_B: Approving alterations to a product baseline
correct_text: Moving an organization from its current way of operating to a target state
why: People-focused change management supports adoption of new ways of working; issues practice handles baseline change control.

stem: What is the main focus of leadership?
option_A: Motivating and influencing people toward project objectives
option_C: Maintaining a register of all risks
correct_text: Motivating and influencing people toward project objectives
why: PRINCE2 distinguishes motivating, influencing leadership from management of agreed tasks and ways of working.

stem: Which activity best represents management rather than leadership?
option_A: Directing the execution of assigned tasks using agreed procedures
option_B: Inspiring stakeholders around a shared outcome
correct_text: Directing the execution of assigned tasks using agreed procedures
why: Management emphasizes instructing and coordinating execution; leadership emphasizes people and motivation.

stem: In PRINCE2, what is co-creation?
option_A: Involving users and key influencers in designing products and ways of working
option_B: Producing products only within the supplier team
option_C: Delegating every project decision to one user
option_D: Rewriting the business case after every meeting
correct_text: Involving users and key influencers in designing products and ways of working
why: Co-creation is purposeful collaboration that improves fit and adoption of products and ways of working.

stem: Which information belongs in the PID communication management approach?
option_A: Who needs information, by what means, and how often feedback is exchanged
option_B: The ranking of every identified risk
option_C: The full set of product test results
correct_text: Who needs information, by what means, and how often feedback is exchanged
why: The communication management approach establishes planned, two-way information flows across the project ecosystem.

stem: Which document describes how affected parts of the business will reach the future organizational state?
why: The change management approach describes the target state and the transition from current to future working practices.

stem: A new service changes routines for staff who are not project team members. What should the project do?
option_A: Engage these people in transition and adoption planning
option_B: Treat them as out of scope for all communications
option_C: Assume the service will be adopted without support
option_D: Include them only in supplier product testing
correct_text: Engage these people in transition and adoption planning
why: People affected by a project are central to successful outcomes, even when outside the formal team.

stem: Which situation most strongly calls for a two-way communication channel?
option_A: Staff need to share concerns about how a new process will work
option_B: The project only needs to publish a completed schedule
option_C: A project archivist needs a read-only copy
option_D: The board receives a previously approved decision
correct_text: Staff need to share concerns about how a new process will work
why: Effective stakeholder engagement listens and receives feedback, not only broadcasts decisions.

stem: Why might a project intentionally build a team with diverse experiences?
option_A: Different capabilities and perspectives help address project needs
option_B: Diversity removes the need for clear roles
option_C: People with identical skills always perform identically
option_D: It ensures no conflict or uncertainty will arise
correct_text: Different capabilities and perspectives help address project needs
why: Effective teams require appropriate, varied capabilities, competencies and perspectives.

stem: Which concept refers to shared values, attitudes and ways of working?
why: Culture influences the behavior and relationships that determine whether change is adopted.

stem: Which is the best example of knowledge sharing in a project ecosystem?
option_A: A workshop where users and suppliers exchange lessons about a new process
option_B: A manager keeps useful lessons in a private notebook
option_C: The project team waits until closure to discuss mistakes
option_D: The board removes feedback sessions to save time
correct_text: A workshop where users and suppliers exchange lessons about a new process
why: People learn valuable lessons socially throughout a project, not only through formal documents.

stem: What is the project ecosystem?
option_A: The network of people and relationships involved in or affected by the project
option_B: The set of only external supplier contracts
option_D: Only the project team’s software tools
correct_text: The network of people and relationships involved in or affected by the project
why: Project success depends on relationships and engagement across the project and organizational ecosystems.

stem: Which consideration is especially important for a dispersed hybrid project team?
option_A: Deliberate communication and team cohesion across locations
option_B: Assuming informal office conversations reach everyone
option_C: Removing stakeholder feedback to speed delivery
correct_text: Deliberate communication and team cohesion across locations
why: Co-located, remote and hybrid teams need suitable channels, trust and coordinated working arrangements.

stem: What is the key purpose of the business case practice?
option_A: To determine whether ongoing investment remains desirable, viable and achievable
option_B: To assign every team member their weekly tasks
option_C: To specify all quality test methods
correct_text: To determine whether ongoing investment remains desirable, viable and achievable
why: The business case practice supports informed investment decisions throughout the project.

stem: A completed online booking platform is delivered. What is this primarily an example of?
why: An output is a deliverable; changed behaviors and measurable improvements may follow after it is used.

stem: Customers start booking appointments online instead of phoning staff. What does this best illustrate?
why: An outcome is the result of change in real-world behavior or circumstances.

stem: The new booking system reduces administrative hours by 25%. How is the measurable improvement classified?
why: A benefit is a measurable improvement from an outcome that contributes to business objectives.

stem: The project decreases waiting times but increases annual electricity use. What should the negative measurable effect be called?
why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline perceived as negative by the investing organization.

stem: Where is the justification for carrying out the project documented?
why: The business case captures justification, weighing estimated costs, expected benefits and risks.

stem: What does the benefits management approach mainly establish?
option_A: Actions and reviews for realizing and measuring expected benefits
option_D: The acceptance criteria for each work package
correct_text: Actions and reviews for realizing and measuring expected benefits
why: Benefits may arise after closure, so planned measurement and ownership are important.

stem: Which product defines planned checks and controls for meeting project sustainability targets?
why: The sustainability management approach specifies actions, reviews and controls for sustainability performance.

stem: When is an outline business case normally developed?
option_C: Only when the first stage exceeds its tolerance
why: Starting up a project establishes sufficient initial justification before significant initiation investment.

stem: At a stage boundary, the project manager re-evaluates how risks affect justification. Which business case technique step is most closely involved?
why: The check step re-examines justification at decision points, including the impact of changed risks and issues.

stem: Which term describes measurable outcomes supporting organizational strategy?
why: Business objectives are measurable strategic outcomes to which project outcomes and benefits contribute.

stem: A project has an agreed range for how much carbon emissions may vary from target. Which tolerance applies?
why: Sustainability is a distinct PRINCE2 performance aspect and its targets and tolerances can support ESG goals.

stem: What question does the organization practice primarily answer?
option_A: Who is accountable and responsible for the project work?
option_B: What is each product’s acceptance score?
option_C: When should supplier invoices be paid?
option_D: How much risk can the organization tolerate?
correct_text: Who is accountable and responsible for the project work?
why: Organization establishes project structures, accountability, responsibilities and relationships.

stem: Which role is the single point of ultimate accountability for project success?
why: The executive is appointed by the business and retains ultimate accountability for success and business justification.

stem: Who represents expected benefits, user needs and adoption on the project board?
why: The senior user represents the user community and benefits, including successful handover and adoption.

stem: Who is accountable for supplier technical integrity and the quality of delivered products?
why: The senior supplier represents the expertise and resources that will deliver the products.

stem: Who manages the project day to day on the board’s behalf?
why: The project manager directs day-to-day management within agreed authority and stage tolerances.

stem: Which role is directly responsible for delivering assigned work-package products?
why: Team managers accept and deliver agreed work packages within the constraints set by the project manager.

stem: Why should project assurance be independent from project support?
option_A: Assurance must provide independent confidence in management and products
option_B: Project support is never allowed to maintain logs
option_D: Project support has sole accountability for benefits
correct_text: Assurance must provide independent confidence in management and products
why: Assurance acts independently of the project manager and its support function.

stem: Who defines the project-level tolerances within which the project board acts?
why: The business layer commissions and constrains the project board; the board sets tolerances for stages.

stem: Which description best fits the work breakdown structure?
option_A: A hierarchy of work linking the product breakdown to work packages
option_B: A chart of only project-board membership
option_C: A set of approved quality specifications
option_D: A prioritized list of user acceptance criteria
correct_text: A hierarchy of work linking the product breakdown to work packages
why: A work breakdown structure connects products to the work needed to deliver them.

stem: Which three roles normally represent the three project interests on the project board?
option_A: Executive, senior user and senior supplier
option_B: Project manager, scheduler and finance assistant
option_D: Project support, risk owner and change authority
correct_text: Executive, senior user and senior supplier
why: The board represents business, user and supplier interests.

stem: Can the same person be both the project executive and project manager?
option_A: No, those two roles must remain separate
option_C: Yes, if a team manager approves
option_D: Yes, if no supplier is external
correct_text: No, those two roles must remain separate
why: The single-point executive accountability cannot be combined with the project manager role.

stem: Which PID element defines the project’s reporting lines and assignment of management roles?
why: The team structure and role descriptions clarify how project accountability and responsibilities are organized.

stem: What is the main purpose of the plans practice?
option_A: To explain what will be delivered and how, by whom, when and for how much
option_B: To approve only changes to baselines
option_C: To define risk appetite for the whole business
correct_text: To explain what will be delivered and how, by whom, when and for how much
why: Plans support communication and control by connecting delivery detail to the project business case.

stem: Which plan gives the high-level view of major project products and their delivery?
why: The project plan provides the overall delivery picture and project-level control baseline.

stem: Which plan provides the detailed basis for controlling a management stage?
why: Stage plans support project manager control in the current stage.

stem: Which plan may be used to organize a team’s activities for an assigned work package?
why: A team plan is optional and can help a team manager plan work-package delivery.

stem: The board asks for a replacement plan after a forecast stage tolerance breach. What type of plan is appropriate?
why: An exception plan proposes how to respond to the exception and may replace the affected plan when approved.

stem: What is described by a work package description?
option_A: How agreed products will be produced and delivered under delegated responsibility
option_B: The full justification for the entire project
option_D: A record of only identified issues
correct_text: How agreed products will be produced and delivered under delegated responsibility
why: Work package descriptions formalize delivery expectations and responsibility passed to a team.

stem: Where are the project-level user quality expectations and acceptance criteria set out?
why: The project product description records expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods for the project product.

stem: What does product-based planning emphasize first?
option_A: Defining the required products before deriving work and schedules
option_B: Allocating all staff before understanding deliverables
option_C: Choosing the earliest finish date then reducing scope
option_D: Writing the risk register instead of defining deliverables
correct_text: Defining the required products before deriving work and schedules
why: The products and their descriptions provide the starting point for estimates, work and schedule.

stem: A team cannot start testing until an external regulator provides approval. What kind of dependency is this?
why: Dependencies can be internal or external; external approvals are outside direct project control.

stem: What is a planning horizon?
option_A: The future period for which planning can reasonably be detailed and reliable
option_B: The time between two checkpoint reports
option_D: The gap between planned and actual benefits
correct_text: The future period for which planning can reasonably be detailed and reliable
why: Plans become less certain further into the future, so near-term stages receive greater detail.

stem: Identify the missing word: A [?] is a sequence or set of timed activities and milestones within a plan.
why: A schedule shows intended activity timing, milestones and dependencies.

stem:
Which TWO statements are correct?
1. Team plans are optional.
2. A project plan is normally more detailed than the current stage plan.
3. An exception plan may replace a plan after a tolerance breach.
4. Product descriptions are unnecessary for product-based planning.
why: Team plans are optional, and exception plans are prepared following an exception; the stage plan is more detailed than the project plan.

stem: What is the purpose of the quality practice?
option_A: To document product requirements and establish how they will be met
option_B: To ensure every change request is approved
option_C: To authorize the project at initiation
option_D: To decide the amount of acceptable financial risk
correct_text: To document product requirements and establish how they will be met
why: Quality aligns products with user requirements and sets up methods for verifying them.

stem: What are acceptance criteria?
option_A: Conditions the project product must satisfy before users accept it
correct_text: Conditions the project product must satisfy before users accept it
why: Acceptance criteria are prioritized requirements for acceptance of the overall project product.

stem: Which description most closely fits quality specifications?
option_A: The measurable quality criteria and levels to apply when checking a product
option_B: The roles of project board members
option_C: The benefits expected after project closure
correct_text: The measurable quality criteria and levels to apply when checking a product
why: Quality specifications make quality checks objective and testable.

stem: What is a requirement in PRINCE2?
option_A: A documented need or expectation recorded in an approved management product
option_B: Any informal comment in a meeting
option_C: A risk that has already occurred
correct_text: A documented need or expectation recorded in an approved management product
why: Requirements are captured and controlled through agreed documentation or management products.

stem: Where are the user’s overall quality expectations for the project product recorded?
why: The project product description establishes what overall quality and acceptance look like.

stem: Testing software against specified response times is an example of which activity?
why: Quality control examines actual products and delivery work against defined standards.

stem: An independent function audits whether the project’s quality system is likely to deliver compliant products. What is this?
why: Quality assurance provides systematic confidence and is typically undertaken independently of the project team.

stem: Which management product records planned and completed quality checks?
why: The quality register tracks quality activities and their results.

stem: Which register tracks a product’s status as it moves toward approval and acceptance?
why: The product register tracks products and key status information; the quality register tracks checks.

stem: What does the quality management approach describe?
option_A: Standards, methods and responsibilities for achieving required quality
option_B: Who approves the project business case
option_C: How the benefits tolerance was calculated
option_D: Which stakeholder owns each risk action
correct_text: Standards, methods and responsibilities for achieving required quality
why: It provides the overarching plan for quality specifications, criteria and controls.

stem: A product passes all required checks and users formally take ownership. Which activity is being completed?
why: Product acceptance confirms that specified acceptance requirements have been met and ownership can transfer.

stem: What should happen if a finished product cannot meet an approved quality specification?
option_A: Raise and assess the off-specification through issue management
option_B: Ignore it if it is within the stage cost tolerance
option_C: Rewrite the product description without control
option_D: Classify it only as an unmaterialized risk
correct_text: Raise and assess the off-specification through issue management
why: A failure or predicted failure to meet specifications is an off-specification, managed as an issue.

stem: What is a risk?
option_A: An uncertain event that could affect project objectives
option_B: An event that has definitely already occurred
option_C: A routine approval with no uncertain outcome
option_D: A product accepted by the user
correct_text: An uncertain event that could affect project objectives
why: A risk concerns uncertainty and may be a threat or an opportunity.

stem: Which management product maintains details and history of identified project risks?
why: Risk register entries track risks and their current status, ownership and responses.

stem: Where are the project’s agreed procedures for managing uncertainty documented?
why: The risk management approach defines techniques, standards, procedures and responsibilities.

stem: Who has overall responsibility for managing and monitoring a specific assigned risk?
why: The risk owner is accountable for the particular risk; action owners carry out assigned response actions.

stem: Who is assigned a particular action such as arranging backup equipment to respond to a risk?
why: A risk action owner owns the execution of a specific agreed response action.

stem: What is risk appetite?
option_A: The amount and type of risk the business is willing to pursue
option_B: The current list of all project risks
option_C: A fixed amount of time for every stage
option_D: The number of risks accepted at closure
correct_text: The amount and type of risk the business is willing to pursue
why: Appetite expresses broad willingness to take risk in pursuit of objectives.

stem: How does risk tolerance differ from risk appetite?
option_A: Tolerance sets measurable limits for objectives exposed to risk
option_C: Tolerance is always a single cash value
option_D: Tolerance records risks that already occurred
correct_text: Tolerance sets measurable limits for objectives exposed to risk
why: Risk tolerance represents a measurable acceptable range for an at-risk objective.

stem: Which combination is used to understand the seriousness of a risk?
why: Risk is assessed by considering its likelihood and effect on objectives, alongside other factors as relevant.

stem: A project decides to change its design so a serious threat can no longer occur. Which response is this?
why: Avoiding removes the threat or its cause, rather than merely reducing likelihood or impact.

stem: A promising new technology could speed delivery. The team acts to make that opportunity more likely. Which response is this?
why: Enhance improves the probability or impact of a beneficial uncertain event.

stem: The team compares risks and prioritizes them based on combined exposure. Which risk technique step is this?
why: Assess analyzes and prioritizes threats and opportunities and their aggregate exposure.

stem: A manager gives too much weight to keeping what they already have when evaluating options. What decision bias is this?
why: Loss aversion can distort choices by valuing avoiding loss more than equivalent potential gains.

stem: What is the purpose of the issues practice?
option_A: To assess issues and control changes to approved baselines
option_B: To remove the need for quality planning
option_C: To define the organization’s strategic objectives
option_D: To evaluate only events that have not occurred
correct_text: To assess issues and control changes to approved baselines
why: The issues practice manages events requiring attention and controls baseline changes.

stem: A required product is known to be unable to meet an approved specification. What issue type is this?
why: An off-specification relates to a product that will not meet agreed quality specifications.

stem: A user proposes adding an extra feature to an approved product. How should the proposal be classified?
why: A request for change proposes modifying an approved baseline.

stem: A supplier has already missed a contractually agreed delivery. Is this best treated as a risk or an issue?
option_A: Issue, because the event has occurred
option_B: Risk, because any delay is uncertain
option_D: No record, because the stage may recover
correct_text: Issue, because the event has occurred
why: Once an event occurs and needs management action, it is an issue rather than a future uncertainty.

stem: What is a project baseline?
option_A: The current approved versions of products subject to change control
option_B: Every draft ever produced during a project
option_C: Only the project’s first cost estimate
option_D: A summary of informal stakeholder opinions
correct_text: The current approved versions of products subject to change control
why: Baselines are approved reference versions against which changes are controlled.

stem: Where should an identified issue and its status normally be tracked?
why: The issue register provides a record of issues and progress toward resolution.

stem: A significant issue needs fuller analysis and a decision recommendation. Which management product is suitable?
why: Issue reports capture detail and support a structured decision on significant issues.

stem: What is a change budget?
option_A: Authorized provision set aside for changes within agreed constraints
option_B: The full budget for all project products
option_C: A reserve used only for realized risks
correct_text: Authorized provision set aside for changes within agreed constraints
why: A change budget supports controlled approval and implementation of authorized changes.

stem: Which sequence best matches the PRINCE2 issue management technique?
why: Issue management moves from recognizing an issue to evaluating choices, authorizing and carrying out action.

stem: What is the first step when a new issue is identified?
option_B: Immediately implement a change to the baseline
option_D: Delete the previous approved product description
why: Capture establishes type, priority and record of the issue before assessment and decision.

stem: Where are the project’s rules for controlling changes to approved products described?
why: The issue management approach covers capturing, reporting, assessing and controlling baseline changes.

stem: Who can authorize a change when authority has been formally delegated and limits are respected?
option_A: The assigned change authority within its delegated limits
option_D: Only an independent auditor, regardless of delegation
correct_text: The assigned change authority within its delegated limits
why: Approval can be delegated, but authority must be clear and decisions remain within agreed constraints.

stem: What is the purpose of the progress practice?
option_A: To compare performance with plans, forecast outcomes and control deviations
option_B: To produce technical specifications for suppliers
option_C: To appoint all project board members
option_D: To write only the initial business case
correct_text: To compare performance with plans, forecast outcomes and control deviations
why: Progress provides control through actual-versus-plan monitoring and forward-looking forecasts.

stem: What is an exception in PRINCE2?
option_A: A forecast deviation beyond an agreed tolerance
option_B: Any difference between actual and planned performance
option_C: Every issue raised by a user
option_D: Any completed product that needs testing
correct_text: A forecast deviation beyond an agreed tolerance
why: An exception occurs when a plan is forecast to exceed a permitted limit, not for every small variance.

stem: What does a tolerance establish?
option_A: The permitted variation within delegated authority
option_C: The minimum number of product descriptions
option_D: The number of management stages permitted
correct_text: The permitted variation within delegated authority
why: Tolerances define when decisions can remain at the current level and when escalation is necessary.

stem: Which is an example of a time-driven control?
option_C: An exception report raised after a forecast breach
why: Time-driven controls operate at regular intervals; event-driven controls are triggered by events.

stem: Which is an example of an event-driven control?
option_A: A board decision at the end of a management stage
option_D: A daily status message at 9 a.m.
correct_text: A board decision at the end of a management stage
why: A stage boundary is a specific event that triggers review and authorization.

stem: Who normally receives checkpoint reports from the team manager?
why: Checkpoint reports communicate work-package progress from the team manager to project manager.

stem: Which report gives the project board periodic updates on the current stage?
why: The project manager uses highlight reports to keep the board informed at an agreed frequency.

stem: Which report is especially useful to the board when deciding whether to authorize another stage?
why: End stage reports summarize stage performance and information needed for future decisions.

stem: What report supports escalating a forecast breach of stage tolerances?
why: An exception report describes the expected breach and its implications for the next management level.

stem: Where might a project manager record an informal note or minor item not otherwise captured?
why: The daily log is a flexible record for informal matters and everyday observations.

stem: How do a lessons log and lessons report differ?
option_A: The log records lessons as they arise; the report shares a synthesized set of lessons
option_B: The log contains only risks; the report contains only benefits
option_C: The report is used exclusively before project initiation
option_D: They are interchangeable names for an issue register
correct_text: The log records lessons as they arise; the report shares a synthesized set of lessons
why: Lessons are captured continuously and can be consolidated for wider learning and future projects.

stem: What should project progress data help the team do beyond reporting past events?
option_A: Forecast future performance and identify emerging deviations
option_B: Eliminate the need for human judgment
option_C: Guarantee that all benefits will be realized
correct_text: Forecast future performance and identify emerging deviations
why: Current, reliable data enables forward-looking decisions and earlier response to potential exceptions.

stem: Which process decides whether a proposed project is worth the effort of full initiation?
why: Starting up checks viability and avoids unnecessary investment in unsuitable project initiation.

stem: Who carries out the directing a project process?
why: The project board provides direction, key decisions and authorization without doing detailed day-to-day management.

stem: Which process establishes solid foundations before major delivery expenditure?
why: Initiating a project develops the PID, full justification, arrangements and project plan.

stem: In which process does the project manager allocate work, review progress and take corrective action during a stage?
why: Controlling a stage is the project manager’s day-to-day coordination and control of stage delivery.

stem: Which process governs accepting, executing and handing over an assigned work package?
why: Managing product delivery is the team-level interface ensuring agreed products are completed.

stem: Which process prepares information so the board can decide whether to authorize the next management stage?
why: Stage boundary management assesses the stage, updates justification and plans the next stage.

stem: Which process checks acceptance and makes arrangements for an orderly project shutdown?
why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, transition, outstanding actions and project performance.

stem: What usually triggers the starting up a project process?
option_A: A project mandate from the commissioning business
correct_text: A project mandate from the commissioning business
why: The project mandate initiates evaluation of the proposed project.

stem: What is normally produced during starting up to justify and plan the initiation stage?
option_A: Project brief and initiation stage plan
option_B: End project report and closure recommendation
option_D: Detailed plans for every later team activity
correct_text: Project brief and initiation stage plan
why: The start-up process assembles the project brief and plans the initiation stage so the board can authorize initiation.

stem: Which management product is a major output of initiating a project?
why: The PID sets out the agreed project foundation: justification, plans, controls and approaches.

stem: Who authorizes the start of a new management stage after reviewing the relevant information?
why: The project board authorizes management stages as part of directing a project.

stem: The team manager reports that the agreed work package is complete. Which process is this part of?
why: Completing and notifying work package completion are core activities in managing product delivery.

stem: When is managing a stage boundary normally first used?
option_A: At the end of the initiation stage
option_B: Only before the project mandate is issued
option_D: After the project has already closed
correct_text: At the end of the initiation stage
why: Stage boundaries normally follow initiation and each subsequent stage except the final stage, with exception planning also possible.

stem: What should the project manager do when the board directs an early project shutdown?
option_A: Use the closing a project process to close it in a controlled way
option_B: Simply abandon all records and products
option_D: Always complete every planned stage first
correct_text: Use the closing a project process to close it in a controlled way
why: Premature closure still requires orderly handover, review and resolution of open items.

stem: Which process covers the board’s authorization of initiation, the project, stages and eventual closure?
why: Directing a project spans the life of the project and covers major board authorization decisions.

stem: Which activity is most closely associated with controlling a stage?
option_A: Authorize a work package for the team to deliver
option_B: Approve the original project mandate on behalf of the business
option_C: Accept ownership of the project product after closure
correct_text: Authorize a work package for the team to deliver
why: The project manager uses controlling a stage to issue work packages and respond to delivery progress.

stem: Which statement about management stages is correct?
option_A: A PRINCE2 project has an initiation stage and at least one subsequent management stage
option_B: The initiation stage is optional on all projects
option_C: A stage must deliver a realized financial benefit
option_D: There can only be one management stage
correct_text: A PRINCE2 project has an initiation stage and at least one subsequent management stage
why: PRINCE2 expects at least two management stages, starting with initiation.

stem: Before requesting project closure, what should the project manager confirm?
option_A: That the product has been accepted and follow-on actions are addressed
option_B: That all future benefits have already been realized
option_C: That no risks were ever recorded
option_D: That stage tolerances have been permanently removed
correct_text: That the product has been accepted and follow-on actions are addressed
why: Closure establishes user acceptance and arrangements for operational support, open risks and post-project reviews.

stem:
Which TWO belong to managing a stage boundary?
1. Review the current stage.
2. Prepare the next stage plan.
3. Direct every daily team activity.
4. Replace the board’s authorization authority.
why: The project manager evaluates the stage and prepares the next-stage information for board decisions.

stem: Which process is primarily about the team manager’s assurance to the project manager that agreed products can be produced?
why: Managing product delivery creates a controlled interface between project manager and product-delivery team.

stem: A university builds a new online portal, then transfers its ongoing operation to its IT department. When does the project cease to be needed?
option_A: After its agreed change and products have been delivered and handed into business as usual
option_B: When the portal first becomes an idea
option_C: When the first developer joins the project
option_D: Only when the portal is permanently retired
correct_text: After its agreed change and products have been delivered and handed into business as usual
why: Projects are temporary. Operational use and support continue as business as usual after the project.

stem: Which set contains exactly the five integrated elements of PRINCE2?
option_A: Principles, people, practices, processes and project context
option_B: People, quality, risk, products and budgets
option_C: Principles, processes, themes, quality and programmes
option_D: Products, programmes, portfolios, practices and plans
correct_text: Principles, people, practices, processes and project context
why: The five integrated elements describe how PRINCE2 works as a whole.

stem: A product team frequently demonstrates partly completed software and improves it using feedback. Which delivery approach fits best?
why: Iterative-incremental delivery refines and develops products through feedback and increments.

stem: Which performance aspect concerns the permissible variation in the products to be delivered?
why: Scope concerns which products are included and the permitted variation in those products.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 distinguish a project from everyday operations?
option_A: Projects create change and uncertainty within a temporary organization
option_B: Project workers are never employed permanently
option_C: Projects have no governance once products are defined
correct_text: Projects create change and uncertainty within a temporary organization
why: The distinctive characteristics are change, temporary, cross-functional, unique and uncertain.

stem: Where does sustainability sit in PRINCE2 7?
option_A: Among the seven aspects of project performance
option_B: Only as an optional operational checklist
correct_text: Among the seven aspects of project performance
why: PRINCE2 7 includes sustainability alongside benefits, costs, time, quality, scope and risk.

stem: Two identical-looking system deployments use different suppliers and stakeholder groups. What does this illustrate?
option_A: Each project is unique in its particular circumstances
option_B: Projects must use a different methodology every time
option_C: Products cannot be reused across projects
option_D: Projects should avoid lessons from prior work
correct_text: Each project is unique in its particular circumstances
why: A project may resemble others but the combination of people, setting, products and timings is unique.

stem: Which is an example of a commercial context?
option_A: A contract that places specialist product delivery with an external supplier
option_C: The design of the lessons log
option_D: How often the team meets informally
correct_text: A contract that places specialist product delivery with an external supplier
why: Commercial arrangements influence how the people, practices and processes are tailored.

stem: The board reviews whether expected benefits still outweigh costs before authorizing the next stage. Which principle is most clearly applied?
why: A project needs ongoing justification; it is not enough to justify it only at start-up.

stem: Which principle makes it reasonable for a manager to take decisions without seeking approval for every small change?
why: Authority is delegated within stated tolerances; a forecast breach triggers escalation.

stem: A small, low-risk project uses brief digital records rather than many long documents while still applying all PRINCE2 principles. What is being demonstrated?
option_C: Assume roles are identical on every project
option_D: Manage only at the end of the project
why: Tailoring adjusts methods and records to fit scale and circumstances, not the seven principles.

stem: When should learning from experience take place?
option_A: Before, throughout and after the project
option_B: Only after the final product is accepted
correct_text: Before, throughout and after the project
why: Relevant previous lessons, current experience and post-project learning are all valuable.

stem: Product acceptance requirements are agreed before a detailed activity schedule is drawn up. Which principle is being applied?
why: Define the deliverable and its quality expectations first, then plan delivery work.

stem: What does manage by stages require?
option_A: The project is planned, monitored and controlled one management stage at a time
option_B: Every stage must have identical length
option_C: All technical delivery must use sequential methods
option_D: A project must have only one stage
correct_text: The project is planned, monitored and controlled one management stage at a time
why: Board decision points divide a project into management stages.

stem: The project manager documents who represents the investors, end users and suppliers, and how they will collaborate. Which principle is prominent?
why: Governance needs agreed accountability and constructive links between stakeholder groups.

stem: The project forecasts a small cost overrun that remains inside the agreed cost tolerance. What is the best general action?
option_A: Manage it within delegated authority and keep monitoring
option_C: Escalate every deviation to the board as an exception
correct_text: Manage it within delegated authority and keep monitoring
why: A deviation is not automatically an exception; tolerances establish when higher-level intervention is needed.

stem: Which group is included in the people element of PRINCE2?
option_A: Those working on a project and those affected by its change
option_B: Only people assigned formal delivery roles
option_D: Only the project board and project manager
correct_text: Those working on a project and those affected by its change
why: The people element explicitly covers the wider project and organizational ecosystems.

stem: Staff in operations must change daily work routines to use a new system. Which approach deals with the transition?
why: The change management approach addresses the move from current to target organizational state.

stem: Which statement most closely describes leadership?
option_A: Motivating, influencing and enabling people toward project objectives
option_B: Merely assigning tasks against a fixed schedule
option_C: Authorizing changes to the project baseline
option_D: Auditing products independently of the project
correct_text: Motivating, influencing and enabling people toward project objectives
why: PRINCE2 distinguishes leadership (motivation, influence, relationships) from management (directing tasks and controls).

stem: A project invites service desk users to help design the new support workflow rather than telling them what will happen. What is this an example of?
why: Co-creation uses users and key influencers in jointly developing products and ways of working to aid adoption.

stem: Which management approach sets out how information and feedback flow across the project ecosystem?
why: The communication management approach identifies stakeholders, channels, frequency and feedback needs.

stem: Two equally qualified team members contribute differently depending on the group they work with. What should the project manager remember?
option_A: Team dynamics and relationships affect performance
option_C: Only the board can improve team collaboration
option_D: People factors cease to matter once roles are assigned
correct_text: Team dynamics and relationships affect performance
why: Capability and competence do not remove the influence of culture, trust, team structure and relationships.

stem: A person who believes they will be affected by the project may be a what?
why: Stakeholders can affect, be affected by, or perceive they are affected by the project.

stem: A project has a remote delivery team spanning several cultures. Which response best supports the people element?
option_A: Agree suitable communication and collaboration methods for the whole team
option_B: Assume co-located meeting rules work unchanged
option_C: Avoid feedback until the end of the project
option_D: Include only employees from one culture
correct_text: Agree suitable communication and collaboration methods for the whole team
why: Teams benefit from cultural awareness, bidirectional communication and suitable ways of working.

stem: What does the business case justify?
option_A: The investment in a project relative to expected benefits, costs, dis-benefits and risks
option_B: Whether the quality register has every test result
option_C: Whether a team plan uses the latest template
option_D: The names of the risk action owners
correct_text: The investment in a project relative to expected benefits, costs, dis-benefits and risks
why: The business case gives the investment argument for starting and continuing.

stem: A retailer installs self-service checkouts, and customers begin processing orders faster. Which is most likely an outcome?
option_A: Customers complete purchases using the new checkout process
correct_text: Customers complete purchases using the new checkout process
why: Outcomes are changes in behaviour or circumstances; the devices are outputs.

stem: What is a benefit?
option_A: A measurable improvement from an outcome viewed as advantageous
option_B: Any product created by the delivery team
option_C: The approval of a work package
option_D: Any uncertainty considered by the board
correct_text: A measurable improvement from an outcome viewed as advantageous
why: A benefit is not a deliverable; it is a measurable advantageous effect from an outcome.

stem: A new platform will reduce processing costs but will permanently require more manual checks in one department. How should the second effect be treated?
option_A: A dis-benefit to assess and manage
option_C: An opportunity risk that must be exploited
correct_text: A dis-benefit to assess and manage
why: A measurable negative effect resulting from an outcome may be a dis-benefit.

stem: Which document defines how benefits will be checked and reviewed after project closure?
why: Benefits are often realized after project closure, so planned benefits reviews need owners and timings.

stem: At the end of a stage, a major regulation changes project costs and risks. Why is the business case reviewed?
option_A: To test whether the proposed investment still remains justified
option_B: To transfer all risks to the supplier
option_C: To replace the project manager automatically
option_D: To avoid preparing the next stage plan
correct_text: To test whether the proposed investment still remains justified
why: Continue-investment decisions depend on up-to-date desirability, viability and achievability.

stem: Which pair best explains the relationship between outputs and benefits?
option_A: Outputs enable changed outcomes, which may generate benefits
option_B: Benefits are the physical items delivered by the team
option_C: Outputs are always measured after project closure
option_D: Benefits must occur before any project output
correct_text: Outputs enable changed outcomes, which may generate benefits
why: PRINCE2 differentiates deliverables, enabled capabilities, changed outcomes and measured effects.

stem: Which approach explains planned actions and controls to meet environmental and social performance targets?
why: Sustainability management covers the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets.

stem: Who is singly accountable for the project success and continued business justification?
why: The executive is a single point of accountability for business investment and justification.

stem: Who represents user needs and is accountable for the specification of benefits?
why: Senior user protects user interests and benefits, including adoption after delivery.

stem: Who represents the delivery expertise and technical integrity of supplier products?
why: The senior supplier represents supplier capability and product technical integrity.

stem: A work package is approved and a delivery team needs day-to-day instructions. Who coordinates and delivers that package?
why: A team manager is accountable for producing allocated products within the work-package agreement.

stem: Who manages day-to-day stage work on behalf of the project board?
why: The project manager controls stages, assigns work and monitors performance within the delegated stage tolerances.

stem: Who appoints the project executive and sets project-level tolerances?
why: The commissioning business level sits outside the project management team and delegates within project tolerances.

stem: Which role must be kept independent of project support to maintain effective assurance?
why: Assurance needs independence and must not be combined with project support.

stem: A project manager also acts as the team manager on a very small project. Is this automatically prohibited?
option_A: No, the roles can be combined if suitable and accountability remains clear
option_B: Yes, the team manager must always be a separate employee
option_C: Yes, because the project manager is above the project board
option_D: No, because the executive can also be the project manager
correct_text: No, the roles can be combined if suitable and accountability remains clear
why: PRINCE2 roles can be tailored; PM and team manager can combine, but executive and PM cannot.

stem: Which three interests must be represented effectively by the project management team?
why: Projects need a business investment view, user-benefit view and supplier-delivery view.

stem: The board authorizes the next stage but delegates detailed work. Who remains accountable to the business for the project?
why: The board directs and remains accountable within the business layer tolerances; it delegates day-to-day managing.

stem: Which plan is the high-level view of products, time and cost across the entire project?
why: The project plan gives the project-wide baseline and major products.

stem: The team manager wants detailed activities and estimates for a work package. Which plan might be useful?
why: A team plan, where useful, helps organize and control team-level work.

stem: Which plan is normally most detailed for managing the currently authorized stage?
why: The stage plan supports project-manager control of stage work; a project plan is higher level.

stem: The current stage plan cannot stay within its time tolerance. The board wants a proposal to replace it. What should be prepared?
why: An exception plan explains the revised way forward after an exception, subject to approval.

stem: In product-based planning, what is the best starting point?
option_B: Pick all activities before identifying deliverables
option_C: Assign every person a fixed daily task
option_D: Set report frequency without identifying products
why: Define what must be delivered and its quality needs before deriving activities and estimates.

stem: A team needs a list of products arranged hierarchically. Which planning aid fits this?
why: The product breakdown structure decomposes what will be produced into a hierarchy.

stem: What is an external dependency?
option_A: A dependency involving something outside the project team’s direct control
option_C: A product description owned by the team
option_D: A quality tolerance set by the team manager
correct_text: A dependency involving something outside the project team’s direct control
why: Dependencies can be internal or external to the project and affect scheduling.

stem: Why can the next stage be planned in more detail than distant later stages?
option_A: Information usually becomes more reliable as work approaches
option_B: Future stages are outside the business case
option_C: Only the initiation stage must have a plan
correct_text: Information usually becomes more reliable as work approaches
why: The planning horizon permits sensible detail in near-term stage plans.

stem: A team documents measurable pass criteria and test methods for a product. What is it defining?
why: Quality specifications state testable measures and thresholds for product quality.

stem: Who normally conducts independent systematic checks of whether the quality arrangements are adequate?
option_B: Product delivery team doing its own tests
option_D: Project support acting as product owner
why: Quality assurance normally operates independently from the project, unlike quality control of products.

stem: What is the purpose of the quality register?
option_A: To record quality activities and their results
correct_text: To record quality activities and their results
why: Quality register tracks quality checks; product register tracks product status.

stem: An agreed acceptance criterion is that an app must work offline. When should this be captured?
option_A: While defining the project product and its acceptance requirements
option_B: Only after the final end project report
option_C: Only if the supplier identifies a risk
option_D: Only when the project board rejects a deliverable
correct_text: While defining the project product and its acceptance requirements
why: Acceptance criteria should be known so products and testing are planned accordingly.

stem: Which record helps answer whether each product has been approved or accepted?
why: Product register summarizes product progression and status.

stem: A software product is forecast not to meet its approved performance standard. What type of issue could this be?
why: An off-specification concerns a product failing or being forecast to fail a specification.

stem: Which is an example of quality control?
option_A: Running agreed acceptance tests on delivered products
correct_text: Running agreed acceptance tests on delivered products
why: Quality control measures the actual products against their specifications.

stem: A user describes their expectation as “simple to navigate,” then agrees an objective response-time target. Which is the more precise testable measure?
why: User expectations are elaborated into measurable specifications and acceptance criteria.

stem: Which is the defining feature of a risk rather than an issue?
option_A: The relevant event is uncertain and may happen in the future
option_B: The event has occurred and needs action
option_C: A baseline has already been changed
option_D: The product has already failed acceptance
correct_text: The relevant event is uncertain and may happen in the future
why: Risk concerns uncertainty, including both threats and opportunities.

stem: Who owns agreed actions to implement a response on behalf of the risk owner?
why: The risk owner takes overall responsibility; the risk action owner implements assigned response actions.

stem: What does risk appetite describe?
option_A: The amount and types of risk an organization is prepared to take
option_B: The sum of all recorded issues
option_C: The maximum time variance in a stage plan
option_D: The final quality criteria for product acceptance
correct_text: The amount and types of risk an organization is prepared to take
why: Risk appetite expresses overall willingness to take risk in pursuit of objectives.

stem: A potential positive event would allow the project to finish early. How should it be classified?
why: Risks include positive opportunities as well as threats.

stem: During which risk management step are threats and opportunities first discovered?
why: The Identify step reviews context and objectives, then records possible risks.

stem: The team pays another party to take on much of the financial consequence of a threat. Which response is being used?
why: Transfer changes who bears an aspect of risk, although management responsibility still requires attention.

stem: What is risk proximity?
option_A: How soon in time a risk might occur
option_B: How quickly its impact is felt after occurrence
option_C: How large its expected cost is
option_D: Who acts for the assigned risk owner
correct_text: How soon in time a risk might occur
why: Proximity is closeness in time; velocity is speed of impact after occurrence.

stem: A team assumes delivery will go perfectly despite evidence of delays. Which bias may be present?
why: Unrealistically favorable assumptions can distort risk decisions and probability assessments.

stem: A user proposes altering an approved reporting requirement. What type of issue is this?
why: A request for change proposes a modification to an approved baseline.

stem: An approved product already fails one of its quality specifications. What type of issue is this?
why: Off-specification records a product that will not meet an approved specification.

stem: Which practice controls amendments to the currently approved project baseline?
why: Issue management includes change control of baselined products.

stem: A project manager receives a change request that exceeds delegated authority. What should happen?
option_A: Escalate it to the appropriate decision authority
option_B: Approve it because it may add benefits
option_C: Record it only as a future risk
correct_text: Escalate it to the appropriate decision authority
why: Change decisions must respect delegated authority and approved constraints.

stem: Which step in the issue management technique evaluates the impact on project objectives?
why: Issues are captured, assessed, recommendations developed, decided and implemented.

stem: An unforeseen regulation already in force creates extra project work. Which label is generally appropriate?
option_B: Uncertain opportunity that has not occurred
why: An event that has occurred and affects project work is an issue, not only a future risk.

stem: Why is a change budget used?
option_A: To fund authorized changes within agreed constraints
option_C: To fund all operations after project closure
correct_text: To fund authorized changes within agreed constraints
why: The change budget makes provision for authorized modifications to a baseline.

stem: An issue has been assessed and possible responses compared. Which stage should come next before implementation?
option_A: Recommend and decide on the response
option_B: Immediately update the baseline without approval
option_C: Transfer all risk to the supplier
correct_text: Recommend and decide on the response
why: The issue technique uses Capture, Assess, Recommend, Decide and Implement.

stem: Who normally sends checkpoint reports about a work package?
why: Checkpoint reports show team delivery progress to the project manager.

stem: A board expects a status report every two weeks. Which report is most relevant?
why: Highlight reports give periodic stage-level information from the project manager to the board.

stem: What makes a forecast an exception?
option_A: A predicted breach of an agreed tolerance
option_B: Any uncertainty listed in the risk register
option_C: Any delivery that happens early within tolerance
option_D: A team meeting that runs long
correct_text: A predicted breach of an agreed tolerance
why: Exception is defined by forecast deviation beyond tolerance, not just any variance.

stem: The project manager forecasts that stage costs will exceed tolerance and needs a board decision. Which report should be prepared?
why: An exception report provides information on the forecast breach for higher-level decision-making.

stem: What is an event-driven control?
option_A: A management control triggered by a defined event
option_C: A meeting scheduled monthly regardless of progress
correct_text: A management control triggered by a defined event
why: Events such as stage boundaries or the issue of an exception report trigger event-driven controls.

stem: At the end of a stage, which report summarizes the stage performance for the board?
why: The end stage report summarizes how the stage performed and supports next-stage decisions.

stem: Which management product evaluates project performance against its original baselines at closure?
why: The end project report evaluates achievement and project performance at closure.

stem: Why should progress systems be used to predict future performance rather than only summarize the past?
option_A: Forecasts allow timely corrective action before delegated limits are exceeded
option_B: Historical performance has no value at all
option_C: Data removes the need for project board decisions
option_D: Project teams cannot use qualitative judgment
correct_text: Forecasts allow timely corrective action before delegated limits are exceeded
why: Progress includes monitoring actuals, forecasting and acting early.

stem: Which process checks whether an idea deserves the investment in project initiation?
why: Start-up checks that a project is worth initiating before extensive preparation.

stem: The project board wants a sound project baseline and management strategies before deciding whether to authorize delivery. Which process prepares these foundations?
why: Initiation develops the PID and business case so the board can authorize the project.

stem: Which process links the project manager and team manager through accepting, executing and delivering work packages?
why: Managing product delivery governs the team-level work package agreement.

stem: A project manager authorizes work packages, checks progress and takes corrective action within stage tolerances. Which process is being used?
why: The project manager uses controlling a stage for day-to-day stage control.

stem: Which process enables a board to authorize the next stage based on actual performance and plans?
why: At boundaries the board needs stage reports, updated plans and business justification.

stem: The board directs an early termination because the project is no longer worthwhile. Which process is still required?
why: The closure process handles controlled premature closure as well as planned closure.

stem: Which process belongs to the project board and spans the project lifecycle?
why: The board directs the project through authorization and major decisions from start-up to closure.

stem: Who authorizes whether another stage should begin?
option_A: Project board using directing a project
option_B: Team manager using managing product delivery
option_C: Project support by updating the daily log
correct_text: Project board using directing a project
why: The project board is the directing level and authorizes major stages.

stem: A warehouse modernization project delivers new scanners and ends after operations adopts them. Which statement fits PRINCE2?
option_A: The project is temporary; the scanners are operated through business as usual after closure
option_B: The project must continue to manage scanning indefinitely
option_C: The project is not unique because scanners existed elsewhere
option_D: Benefits must all be realized before project initiation
correct_text: The project is temporary; the scanners are operated through business as usual after closure
why: Project work creates change temporarily; operational management normally continues after the project closes.

stem: The project uses sequential building work followed by iterative user testing. Which description is strongest?
option_A: A hybrid delivery approach combines delivery methods
option_B: It must be a purely linear-sequential project
option_C: It cannot use PRINCE2 if feedback changes requirements
option_D: The work is an ongoing operational process
correct_text: A hybrid delivery approach combines delivery methods
why: PRINCE2 is a governance method and can sit alongside hybrid delivery methods.

stem: Which factor is part of project context rather than a PRINCE2 practice?
option_A: Whether external contracts and commercial arrangements constrain the project
option_B: How the quality register records planned tests
option_C: Which report is sent by a team manager
option_D: How exceptions are raised to the project board
correct_text: Whether external contracts and commercial arrangements constrain the project
why: Context includes the organizational, commercial, delivery, sustainability and scale circumstances within which PRINCE2 is applied.

stem: Which project performance aspect asks whether products can deliver measurable improvements?
why: Benefits address the value expected from outcomes, not merely whether a product was manufactured correctly.

stem: A project changes a digital service to reduce paper use. Which performance dimension considers that reduction target?
why: PRINCE2 7 expressly includes sustainability among seven aspects to be managed, with performance targets and tolerances.

stem: A supplier delivers a completed database. What is the database itself in the output-outcome-benefit chain?
why: The database is a deliverable. Using it may create outcomes, which may in turn lead to measurable benefits.

stem: A steering group wants to omit 'learn from experience' because the project is small. How should PRINCE2 be tailored?
option_A: Keep every principle and simplify the associated management detail
option_B: Omit the principle if at least three stages remain
option_C: Replace principles with only a project plan
option_D: Obtain permission to omit every other principle
correct_text: Keep every principle and simplify the associated management detail
why: The seven principles remain obligations even when documents, controls and processes are scaled.

stem: A manager can authorize corrective action within agreed boundaries. What makes this possible?
option_A: Delegated tolerances under manage by exception
option_B: A promise never to exceed the stage budget
option_C: Approval by all users for every change
correct_text: Delegated tolerances under manage by exception
why: Explicit tolerances determine the limits within which decisions can be made locally.

stem: A project team revisits a previous failed handover and updates its transition approach. Which principle is demonstrated?
why: Seeking and applying lessons during the project is central to learn from experience.

stem: A new supplier is brought onto the board to represent specialist delivery interests. Which principle is most directly supported?
why: Governance should represent business, user and supplier interests, including external suppliers where appropriate.

stem: Why does the project board make an authorization decision at a management-stage boundary?
option_A: To review performance and business justification before more investment
option_B: To delegate all organizational responsibilities permanently
option_C: To remove the need for product acceptance
option_D: To ensure every stage has equal duration
correct_text: To review performance and business justification before more investment
why: Manage by stages divides management into reviewable control points and enables decisions on continued investment.

stem: An organization calls the business case its 'investment rationale'. What makes the terminology tailoring acceptable?
option_A: The necessary justification and accountability are still established and retained
option_B: Names must always be exactly as in the manual
option_C: Renaming allows business justification to be skipped
option_D: A supplier may unilaterally remove the project board
correct_text: The necessary justification and accountability are still established and retained
why: Tailoring can adapt language to context while retaining the method's principles and purposes.

stem: When is it appropriate to define the acceptance criteria for the final product?
option_A: Before detailed activities are estimated, to maintain focus on required products
option_B: Only after the final stage is complete
option_D: Only when the supplier requests payment
correct_text: Before detailed activities are estimated, to maintain focus on required products
why: Focus on products emphasizes requirements and quality expectations before detailed activity planning.

stem: A hospital introduces a scheduling system, but clinicians resist new shift routines. Which PRINCE2 element needs explicit attention?
option_C: The risk register with no stakeholder involvement
option_D: The project plan's cost estimates alone
why: Project outcomes rely on adoption by affected people; a change management approach plans the move toward the target state.

stem: Which activity is an example of management rather than leadership?
option_A: Instructing team members on the agreed execution of tasks
option_B: Inspiring users to adopt a new process
option_C: Influencing stakeholders to agree a shared goal
option_D: Motivating a diverse team to collaborate
correct_text: Instructing team members on the agreed execution of tasks
why: PRINCE2 distinguishes execution of agreed ways of working (management) from motivating and influencing people (leadership).

stem: Why might a project need to engage someone who has no formal project role?
option_A: They can still affect or be affected by the project
option_B: Only project board members count as stakeholders
option_C: Their involvement removes the need for quality control
correct_text: They can still affect or be affected by the project
why: The stakeholder definition includes affected or influential people outside the project organization.

stem: A remote software team asks users to design the rollout workflow together. Which concept best applies?
why: Co-creation brings users and influencers into developing products and agreed ways of working to improve adoption.

stem: What should a communication management approach include beyond sending progress reports?
option_A: Two-way feedback, audiences, channels and frequency
option_D: The exact time all future risks will occur
correct_text: Two-way feedback, audiences, channels and frequency
why: Communication supports alignment and bidirectional engagement across project and organizational ecosystems.

stem: A project asks employees to explain which interim operating changes they need before launch. Which approach should capture this?
why: Change management covers current, interim and target organizational states and the route between them.

stem: Which factor can influence how a highly capable individual performs in a project team?
option_B: Their qualifications determine identical results in every team
option_C: Only the project manager's job title
option_D: Only whether work uses a hybrid lifecycle
why: PRINCE2 7 stresses team dynamics, effective relationships, diversity and cultural context.

stem: A new booking platform is deployed, but customers have not started using it. Which statement is correct?
option_A: The platform is an output; benefits depend on outcomes from its use
option_B: The platform automatically proves the planned benefit
option_C: Customer adoption is irrelevant once the output is delivered
correct_text: The platform is an output; benefits depend on outcomes from its use
why: PRINCE2 distinguishes delivered outputs from changed behavior and measurable benefits.

stem: What is an example of a measurable dis-benefit?
option_A: Customers experience an extra two-minute wait after the new process is introduced
option_B: A possible data breach that has not occurred
option_C: An extra feature requested but not approved
option_D: A product that has not yet been tested
correct_text: Customers experience an extra two-minute wait after the new process is introduced
