why: A dis-benefit is a measurable negative effect of an outcome, distinct from an uncertain risk or issue.

stem: A project has stopped meeting the strategic objectives that justified its investment. What should drive the decision to continue?
option_A: Review the current business case and continued business justification
option_B: The age of the initial project mandate alone
correct_text: Review the current business case and continued business justification
why: Investment decisions require the project to remain desirable, viable and achievable.

stem: A business case expects savings to occur one year after the project ends. Which approach plans their measurement?
why: The benefits management approach sets out how and when benefits reviews and related management actions will occur, including after closure.

stem: Which management product sets out actions for the project's sustainability targets?
why: The sustainability management approach provides actions, reviews and controls for sustainability performance targets.

stem: If operating costs rise sharply, what should be reassessed in the business case?
option_A: Whether expected benefits still justify total costs and risk
option_B: Only which member writes checkpoint reports
option_D: Whether the risk owner can approve product acceptance
correct_text: Whether expected benefits still justify total costs and risk
why: Business-case justification should be kept current when costs, benefits or threats change.

stem: Which pair best describes output and outcome?
option_A: Output is a deliverable; outcome is a result of change in behavior or circumstances
option_B: Output is always a monetary benefit; outcome is always a software product
option_C: Output is uncertainty; outcome is a quality criterion
option_D: Output is a management stage; outcome is a project role
correct_text: Output is a deliverable; outcome is a result of change in behavior or circumstances
why: A delivered product enables change, and that change creates outcomes; those outcomes can bring benefits or dis-benefits.

stem: A carbon-emissions target is expressed with a permissible range. How should the project consider that range?
option_B: Only as an optional user preference
option_C: As a risk action owner's salary
why: PRINCE2 7 includes sustainability as a managed performance target with tolerances, documented in the business justification.

stem: The project board asks who is ultimately accountable for the project and business case. Who is the single named role?
why: The executive is the single point of accountability and owns continued business justification; the executive role cannot be shared.

stem: A supplier's product could be technically defective. Which board role primarily represents the supplier interest and technical integrity?
why: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier-side product quality and the project's technical integrity.

stem: Who represents the user community and is closely concerned with expected benefits and adoption?
why: The senior user represents user needs, adoption, requirements and the specification/realization of benefits.

stem: A work package is forecast to exceed its tolerance. Who should the team manager inform for a management decision?
why: The team manager operates within constraints agreed by the project manager and raises work package problems to that managing level.

stem: The project manager is asked to perform independent assurance over their own work. What is the issue?
option_A: Assurance should remain independent of the work being assured
option_B: The board cannot appoint project assurance
option_D: Project assurance always replaces quality control
correct_text: Assurance should remain independent of the work being assured
why: Project assurance represents independent review for the board and should not be performed by the same person whose work it assesses.

stem: Which role can the project manager potentially also fulfil when the project is small?
option_C: Senior user on behalf of every customer
option_D: Independent project assurance over their own work
why: The project manager may also undertake team management or support roles when appropriate, but must not be the executive or compromise independent assurance.

stem: Which layer appoints the project executive and sets project-level tolerances?
why: The commissioning business sets the outer project limits and appoints the executive.

stem: How does a work breakdown structure differ from a project management team structure?
option_A: It organizes work in a hierarchy; the team structure shows governance roles and lines of authority
option_B: It shows only business benefits; the team structure shows only risks
option_C: Both are simply alternative names for the risk register
option_D: One is used only after project closure
correct_text: It organizes work in a hierarchy; the team structure shows governance roles and lines of authority
why: The WBS organizes project work and connects products to work packages, whereas the team structure describes organization and accountability.

stem: A project board wants to delegate change approval within agreed limits. Which arrangement supports this?
option_A: A defined change authority with delegated limits
option_B: Requiring every supplier to approve any change
option_C: Replacing the project manager with project support
option_D: Omitting change control once delivery begins
correct_text: A defined change authority with delegated limits
why: Authority for changes can be delegated, but the delegation and constraints must be defined.

stem: A programme director asks when the major products are expected over the full lifecycle. Which plan is most suitable?
why: The project plan provides high-level information on major products, times and costs for the whole project.

stem: The project manager needs a detailed control baseline for the next management stage. Which product is needed?
why: A stage plan supports management and control of work within the particular management stage.

stem: A team manager proposes a task-level schedule for a work package. Is a team plan always mandatory?
option_A: No; a team plan is optional and used when useful for organizing a team's work
option_B: Yes; every project must have one team plan per team member
option_C: No; because work packages cannot be planned
option_D: Yes; it replaces the project plan
correct_text: No; a team plan is optional and used when useful for organizing a team's work
why: PRINCE2 uses project, stage and optional team plans; work package descriptions agree delegated work.

stem: Why begin product-based planning with products rather than estimated tasks?
option_A: Clarifying the deliverables enables better estimates, dependencies and schedules
option_B: Tasks are always more important than acceptance criteria
option_C: Product definitions remove the need for quality checks
option_D: Planning is only needed after project completion
correct_text: Clarifying the deliverables enables better estimates, dependencies and schedules
why: Products and their descriptions should drive the subsequent work, effort, dependency and schedule planning.

stem: What should a project product description include?
option_A: User quality expectations and acceptance criteria for the overall project product
option_B: Only the project's planned advertising spend
correct_text: User quality expectations and acceptance criteria for the overall project product
why: The project product description defines the overall delivered product and how acceptance will be judged.

stem: A predecessor system needs to be operational before data migration can start. What planning concept is illustrated?
why: Dependencies express relationships between activities or products that affect sequencing and scheduling.

stem: An agreed stage plan will no longer be viable due to a forecast exception. What is an appropriate planning response following direction?
option_A: Prepare an exception plan to replace the relevant plan if requested
option_B: Continue the old plan as though nothing changed
option_D: Issue only a benefits management approach
correct_text: Prepare an exception plan to replace the relevant plan if requested
why: An exception plan is prepared to show a viable way forward following an exception when the relevant authority requests it.

stem: A team estimates detailed delivery work two years in advance even though requirements remain uncertain. Which guidance is relevant?
option_A: Planning horizon: plan current work in more detail and later work at a suitable higher level
option_B: All stages require equal detail at project initiation
option_C: Detail should only be added after closure
option_D: Products are irrelevant to near-term planning
correct_text: Planning horizon: plan current work in more detail and later work at a suitable higher level
why: Planning horizons recognize that near work can be planned more reliably than distant, uncertain work.

stem: Which document identifies a product's specific quality measures and the finished levels that must be achieved?
why: A product description captures quality specifications and relevant quality methods for its product.

stem: A tester checks whether a completed component meets the approved specification. Which activity is this?
why: Quality control evaluates compliance of specific products against their quality specifications.

stem: An independent function checks whether the project's quality system is suitable and being followed. Which concept is this?
option_B: Quality control of an individual product
why: Quality assurance is generally managed independently and provides confidence that quality requirements will be met.

stem: A final product must satisfy a prioritized set of conditions before the customer accepts it. What are these conditions?
why: Acceptance criteria determine whether the overall project product is acceptable to the user.

stem: A colleague calls any nice-to-have quality preference an approved requirement. What distinction matters?
option_A: A requirement is a documented need or expectation in an approved management product
option_B: Any suggestion becomes a baseline without approval
option_C: Requirements and emerging risks are always identical
option_D: Only supplier requests count as requirements
correct_text: A requirement is a documented need or expectation in an approved management product
why: PRINCE2 distinguishes agreed and documented requirements from general expectations or unapproved suggestions.

stem: The project manager wants an overview of the current delivery status of individual products. What would support this?
why: The product register tracks product status across the project; the quality register tracks quality activities and their results.

stem: The team wants to record scheduled testing, when it happened and its outcome. Which register is appropriate?
why: The quality register records planned and completed quality activities and results.

stem: A product fails an agreed test. What is the next general requirement?
option_A: Record the result and manage the failure using the agreed quality and issue arrangements
option_B: Automatically accept the product because testing was performed
option_D: Ignore the result if the project is on time
correct_text: Record the result and manage the failure using the agreed quality and issue arrangements
why: Quality checks create evidence; failures require controlled resolution rather than silent acceptance.

stem: A storm might delay equipment shipment next month. Why is this a risk rather than an issue?
option_A: It is an uncertain future event that could affect objectives
option_B: It has already occurred and needs issue resolution
option_C: It is an approved change to the baseline
option_D: It is a deliverable awaiting acceptance
correct_text: It is an uncertain future event that could affect objectives
why: Risk concerns uncertain events; an issue is an event or concern that requires management consideration.

stem: What distinguishes the risk owner from the risk action owner?
option_A: The owner manages the whole risk; the action owner performs assigned response actions
option_B: The risk action owner alone funds the entire project
option_C: Both are automatically the project executive
option_D: Only the action owner may record new risks
correct_text: The owner manages the whole risk; the action owner performs assigned response actions
why: The risk owner monitors and controls overall assigned risk, while an action owner implements particular agreed actions.

stem: A team takes steps to make a favorable uncertain event more likely. Which opportunity response is used?
why: Enhance increases the probability or impact of an opportunity, unlike avoid and reduce which describe typical threat responses.

stem: A project redesigns a solution so a particular threat can no longer occur. Which response is this?
why: Avoiding a threat removes its cause or effect on the project, rather than simply reducing its likelihood.

stem: The board sets the overall amount and type of uncertainty it is willing to pursue. What is this?
why: Risk appetite expresses the organization's willingness to take risk in pursuit of objectives.

stem: What does risk tolerance define?
option_A: A measurable acceptable threshold for an objective exposed to risk
option_B: The minimum number of team managers
option_D: The duration of an initiation stage
correct_text: A measurable acceptable threshold for an objective exposed to risk
why: Risk tolerance uses measurable thresholds to bound how much variation is tolerable.

stem: A risk could occur in two weeks and damage service continuity within minutes. Which pairing is correct?
option_A: Proximity: two weeks; velocity: within minutes
option_B: Proximity: within minutes; velocity: two weeks
option_C: Both are types of issue report
option_D: Both refer only to monetary impact
correct_text: Proximity: two weeks; velocity: within minutes
why: Proximity is how near an uncertain event might occur; velocity is how quickly its effect would be felt once it occurred.

stem: During which risk technique step should the team assess and prioritize identified threats and opportunities?
why: The risk technique identifies risks, assesses them, plans responses, implements actions and communicates throughout.

stem: A customer asks to modify the agreed interface of an approved product. What type of issue is this?
option_B: Risk that has not yet been identified
why: A proposed amendment to a baselined product is a request for change and follows issue/change control.

stem: A feature will not satisfy its approved quality specification. Which issue type fits best?
why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its agreed quality specifications.

stem: A system integration failure has happened and is blocking testing. What best describes it?
option_A: A problem requiring current management action
option_D: Only a change to the business case
correct_text: A problem requiring current management action
why: The event has occurred and has negative impact; issue management deals with problems that require action.

stem: A supplier proposes an unexpected improvement that could save operational costs. Which issue type may apply?
why: An unanticipated positive possibility arising during delivery can be managed as a business-opportunity issue.

stem: What is meant by project baseline?
option_A: The approved versions of controlled project and management products
option_B: Any unsigned idea discussed at a meeting
correct_text: The approved versions of controlled project and management products
why: Baselined products are the approved current versions against which changes are controlled.

stem: An issue has been logged and the team needs to understand its impact on cost, scope and justification. Which step follows?
option_D: Skip straight to a new mandate
why: Issue management examines impact before recommending options and authorizing decisions.

stem: A change authority is given a limited budget to authorize small changes. What matters most?
option_A: Its delegated limits and approved change budget must be observed
option_B: It automatically replaces the project board entirely
option_C: It can rewrite every project-level tolerance
option_D: It cannot approve any change once established
correct_text: Its delegated limits and approved change budget must be observed
why: Decision rights and change budgets may be delegated subject to agreed constraints.

stem: Which management product captures a significant issue's options, assessment and recommendation?
why: The issue report records a particular significant issue for decision and resolution; the issue register tracks issues across the project.

stem: The project manager has approved a change within delegated authority. What follows in the issue technique?
option_A: Implement the authorized change and update controlled records
option_B: Treat the change as a new uncertain risk only
option_C: Ask the senior user to cancel every test
correct_text: Implement the authorized change and update controlled records
why: Issue management uses capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement; implementation updates the relevant baseline.

stem: A team manager sends a regular work-package status report to the project manager. What is it?
why: Checkpoint reports communicate team/work-package progress to the project manager.

stem: A project manager provides the board with a regular summary of stage status. What is it?
why: Highlight reports are regular summaries of stage status from the project manager to the project board.

stem: At a management-stage boundary the board needs a summary of performance against the stage plan. Which report supports the decision?
why: End stage reports review the stage and inform the board before a decision to proceed.

stem: A tolerance is forecast to be exceeded but has not actually been breached yet. What does PRINCE2 call the situation?
why: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond agreed tolerances; escalation should not wait for actual overspend or delay.

stem: A team manager raises a forecast work-package tolerance breach. To which level should it ordinarily go first?
why: Exception control escalates first to the next appropriate management level for work-package tolerances.

stem: A project manager expects a stage to exceed tolerance. Which report informs the board?
why: An exception report presents the forecast deviation and its implications to the directing level.

stem: Which is an example of an event-driven control?
option_A: The project board reviewing an end stage report at a stage boundary
option_B: Issuing a highlight report every Friday
option_C: Checking the team's status each morning
option_D: Holding a monthly risk meeting regardless of events
correct_text: The project board reviewing an end stage report at a stage boundary
why: Event-driven controls occur at specified events; time-driven controls operate at a regular interval.

stem: Which management product is most useful for recording lessons for later application?
why: The lessons log captures lessons as they emerge, supporting learning during and across projects.

stem: What should a forecast do beyond reporting what happened last week?
option_A: Estimate future performance against objectives and tolerances
option_B: Only copy the previous day's checkpoint report
option_D: Guarantee all uncertainties will not occur
correct_text: Estimate future performance against objectives and tolerances
why: The progress practice compares actual achievements with plans and forecasts the likely future position.

stem: What should be decided during starting up a project before committing significant initiation resources?
option_A: Whether the project is sufficiently worthwhile to initiate
option_B: Whether every final benefit has already been realized
option_C: Whether the final product is accepted
option_D: Whether all technical work is complete
correct_text: Whether the project is sufficiently worthwhile to initiate
why: Starting up assesses whether there is enough justification to invest in initiating the project.

stem: Which process prepares the project initiation documentation and detailed justification?
why: Initiating a project establishes the firm foundations and approaches used to manage the project.

stem: Which process allows the project board to retain strategic direction while delegating day-to-day management?
why: Directing a project is the board's governance process, operating through authorizations and exception decisions.

stem: Which process primarily enables the project manager to assign and monitor work during a stage?
why: Controlling a stage covers assigning work packages, reviewing stage status, dealing with issues and communicating progress.

stem: A team manager has accepted an agreed work package and is coordinating its delivery. Which process is being applied?
why: Managing product delivery governs the interface between the project manager's authorization and the team's accepted delivery commitments.

stem: The project manager is asked to prepare the next stage plan and refresh the business case. Which process handles this?
why: The stage boundary process prepares the evidence and next-stage planning needed for board authorization.

stem: Users have accepted the final product. What process coordinates handover, lessons and the end project report?
why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, records project performance and provides controlled closure.

stem: A project must stop early because its justification has disappeared. Which process still applies to an authorized premature closure?
option_D: Managing product delivery must continue to completion
why: PRINCE2 uses a controlled closing process even when the project ends prematurely.

stem: Which process starts before project initiation and is used to prevent unsuitable projects proceeding?
why: Startup gives decision-makers enough information to determine whether initiation is justified.

stem: Which statement about directing a project is correct?
option_A: Board direction runs from early authorization decisions through project closure
option_B: It is performed only inside the initiation stage
option_C: It ends as soon as the first stage plan is approved
option_D: It is the same as the team manager's daily product delivery
correct_text: Board direction runs from early authorization decisions through project closure
why: The directing process provides ongoing governance over the project lifecycle.

stem:
Which TWO statements about projects are correct?
1. They are temporary.
2. They are always identical to past projects.
3. They introduce uncertainty.
4. They are the same as ongoing business as usual.
why: PRINCE2 identifies change, temporary nature, uniqueness, cross-functional work and uncertainty as distinguishing project characteristics.

stem:
Which TWO statements about tailoring PRINCE2 are correct?
1. Terminology can reflect the organization's language.
2. One of the seven principles may be deleted.
3. Controls can be scaled for complexity.
4. Every project needs identical paperwork.
why: Tailoring can adapt terminology, management products and control detail, but does not remove the seven principles.

stem:
Which TWO statements about people are correct?
1. Stakeholders can include people affected by the project who do not work on it.
2. Leadership only means instructing tasks.
3. Co-creation involves users and influencers in design.
4. Every stakeholder must be on the project board.
why: The people element includes impacted stakeholders; leadership goes beyond management instruction and co-creation improves adoption.

stem:
Which TWO statements about value are correct?
1. An output is a deliverable.
2. A benefit is a measurable improvement from an outcome.
3. Every outcome is automatically a financial benefit.
4. A dis-benefit is always an uncertain risk.
why: Outputs can enable changed outcomes; those changes can produce measurable benefits and dis-benefits.

stem:
Which TWO role statements are correct?
1. One project executive is ultimately accountable for project success.
2. Senior supplier defines all user benefits.
3. Senior user represents the interests of users and expected benefits.
4. The team manager must always sit on the project board.
why: The executive owns business accountability; the senior user focuses on requirements, adoption and benefits; supplier interests sit with senior supplier.

stem:
Which TWO statements about plans are correct?
1. A team plan is optional.
2. A project plan is a detailed daily task schedule for every stage.
3. A stage plan is a detailed control baseline for a management stage.
4. An exception plan can never replace a stage plan.
why: A project plan is high level for the whole project; a stage plan is detailed, and an optional team plan may support a work package.

stem:
Which TWO quality statements are correct?
1. Quality assurance is generally independent of the project team.
2. Quality control checks specific products against their requirements.
3. Acceptance criteria only concern time and cost.
4. Requirements cannot be revised under approved change control.
why: Product tests are quality control; systematic independent confidence in the arrangements is quality assurance.

stem:
Which TWO statements about risks are correct?
1. A threat could harm objectives if it happens.
2. An opportunity could help objectives if it happens.
3. Every risk has already occurred.
4. Every risk action owner must be the executive.
why: A risk is uncertain and may be a threat or an opportunity; owners and action owners can be assigned as appropriate.

stem:
Which TWO issue statements are correct?
1. A request for change proposes an alteration to an approved baseline.
2. Off-specification means a product will not meet its specification.
3. Every issue is merely an uncertain future risk.
4. All issues require a board-approved exception plan.
why: Change requests and off-specifications are issue types; responses and approvals depend on impact and delegated authority.

stem:
Which TWO statements about progress reports are correct?
1. A checkpoint report can go from team manager to project manager.
2. A highlight report can go from project manager to project board.
3. Exception reports are only made after actual tolerance breaches.
4. An end project report is prepared before starting up.
why: Time-driven checkpoint and highlight reports connect the levels; exceptions are forecast deviations beyond tolerance.

stem:
Which TWO statements about processes are correct?
1. Directing a project is mainly a project board process.
2. Managing product delivery is run by the project board to authorize stage boundaries.
3. Controlling a stage is mainly a project manager process.
4. Closing a project is performed before initiating a project.
why: Board-level direction is distinct from project manager stage control and team-level product delivery.

stem: Identify the missing words: Risk [?] describes how close in time an uncertain risk event may occur.
why: Proximity refers to how near in time a risk may occur; velocity measures how quickly its effects arise afterward.

stem: Identify the missing words: A forecast deviation beyond an agreed tolerance is an [?].
why: PRINCE2 escalates a forecast exception; it is not necessary to wait for the deviation to happen.

stem: Identify the missing words: The [?] is the single role ultimately accountable for project success and business justification.
why: The executive is appointed by the business and is ultimately accountable for project success.

stem: Identify the missing words: A proposal to modify a project baseline is a request for [?].
why: A request for change is an issue type involving an approved project baseline.

stem: Which action is NOT normally an example of quality control?
option_A: Independently evaluating the overall quality management system
option_B: Testing a finished product against its agreed tolerances
option_C: Checking a component meets its specifications
correct_text: Independently evaluating the overall quality management system
why: Independent systematic evaluation of quality arrangements is quality assurance, while product checks and tests are quality control.

stem: Which is NOT a purpose of closing a project?
option_A: Authorizing every work package for the next stage
option_B: Confirming the project product is accepted
option_C: Reviewing performance against the project's baselines
option_D: Preparing the end project report and follow-on recommendations
correct_text: Authorizing every work package for the next stage
why: Closing confirms acceptance, evaluates delivery and makes an orderly handover rather than starting another delivery stage.

stem: A retailer runs its existing tills every day and separately forms a temporary team to launch a new checkout system. Which activity is a project?
option_A: Both activities, because they involve staff
option_C: The temporary launch team delivering the new system
option_D: Neither activity, because retail systems are business operations
correct_text: The temporary launch team delivering the new system
why: The team is temporary, cross-functional and has a specific change and product to deliver.

stem: A construction project completes a fixed building phase, then improves a visitor-booking application in short cycles. Which delivery approach best describes this combination?
why: Hybrid combines different specialist delivery approaches within one project; governance stays in place.

stem: A project proposes faster service but will consume significantly more electricity. Which performance aspect makes the increased energy use directly relevant?
why: Sustainability assesses agreed environmental, social and governance performance targets.

stem: A board reviews a new forecast and decides to stop the project because expected value no longer justifies additional cost. Which principle is decisive?
why: The justification must remain desirable, viable and achievable; a project can be stopped when it no longer is.

stem: A project manager discovers a previous team failed to train users. She changes the current handover plan and shares the result. Which principle is most clearly applied?
why: The team identifies a useful lesson, applies it and shares the improved approach.

stem: A very small project has digital combined records but retains all seven guiding obligations and an agreed approval path. Which statement is correct?
option_A: It is not PRINCE2 unless each document has its own printed file
option_B: PRINCE2 principles may be omitted when cost is low
option_C: Only the board can write the management records
option_D: This can be valid tailoring if the board approves the proposed approach
correct_text: This can be valid tailoring if the board approves the proposed approach
why: The formality and detail may be tailored, provided the required principles and control decisions remain.

stem: Users receive a new system on time but reject it because their daily process was not redesigned. Which management approach most directly addresses the missing preparation?
why: Change management prepares affected people and business processes to move to target ways of working.

stem: A remote project sends weekly updates to executives but never asks front-line users for feedback. What is missing from the people element?
why: The communication approach should allow feedback from people affected and critical to success.

stem: A project leader brings employees and key influencers into designing the new work process so they will adopt it. What concept best describes this?
why: Co-creation is collaborative design involving users and key influencers to support adoption.

stem: A clinic installs electronic check-in kiosks. Waiting time later falls by seven minutes on average. Which item is the benefit?
option_B: The ability to check in electronically
option_C: The measured seven-minute reduction in waiting time
option_D: The training materials given to receptionists
correct_text: The measured seven-minute reduction in waiting time
why: The measured reduction is an improvement produced by changed behaviour and supports a business objective.

stem: A digital project should reduce paper use but is expected to increase annual electricity costs. What should the business case do with the increase?
option_A: Ignore it because the project is environmentally positive overall
option_B: Record and assess it as a potential dis-benefit or ongoing cost
option_C: Hide it in the stage plan until closing
option_D: Treat it automatically as a risk that may never occur
correct_text: Record and assess it as a potential dis-benefit or ongoing cost
why: A foreseeable ongoing negative consequence or cost needs explicit analysis in the justification.

stem: A project has closed. Who should use which approach to schedule checks that forecast benefits have actually occurred?
option_A: Project manager using the issue register
option_B: Team manager using a team plan
option_D: Relevant business owners using the benefits management approach
correct_text: Relevant business owners using the benefits management approach
why: The benefits management approach sets actions and reviews, and benefits may require business ownership after closure.

stem: Before the project board begins governing a new programme portal, who is responsible for setting project-level tolerances?
why: The commissioning business layer establishes project tolerances within which the board directs.

stem: The project has one person accountable for continued value and investment, but several people represent different user communities. Which statement is correct?
option_A: There can be multiple executives if there are multiple users
option_B: The project manager must also be the executive
option_C: There is one executive but potentially multiple senior users
option_D: The senior supplier must chair all user meetings
correct_text: There is one executive but potentially multiple senior users
why: There must be one executive; more than one senior user can represent a complex user community.

stem: A project support officer is asked to provide independent assurance of the project manager’s work. Why is this problematic?
option_A: All project support roles must be external suppliers
option_B: Independent project assurance must remain separate from project support
option_C: Only the project manager can perform project assurance
option_D: Project assurance never considers the quality of products
correct_text: Independent project assurance must remain separate from project support
why: Project support provides assistance to day-to-day management, while assurance must examine it independently on behalf of the board.

stem: A project manager needs to tell the board how all major project products, costs and dates fit together, before detailing the next stage. Which plan is appropriate?
why: The project plan gives the high-level picture of products, timing and cost across the project.

stem: A team is told to estimate programming tasks before anybody agrees what the finished service must do. Which planning principle is at risk?
why: Product-based planning should specify deliverables and quality criteria before estimating work.

stem: Stage work is forecast to exceed its cost tolerance. The board requests a realistic replacement for the stage plan. What should the project manager prepare?
why: An exception plan shows how to respond to the forecast breach and may replace the existing stage plan after approval.

stem: A tester measures the response time of a newly built portal against the target in its product description. Which activity is this?
why: Quality control checks the actual product against defined quality specifications.

stem: Users will only accept the finished mobile service if it passes a specified set of prioritised conditions. What are these conditions called?
why: Acceptance criteria define the conditions the overall project product must satisfy for user acceptance.

stem: The project manager wants to know which products have been formally approved and which remain in testing. What record is designed for that overview?
why: The product register records product identity, status and approvals through delivery.

stem: A possible future supplier strike could delay deployment. It has not happened yet. Which practice should assess its probability and impact?
why: The risk practice identifies and assesses uncertainty, including threats and opportunities.

stem: A risk owner approves the overall response plan and asks a colleague to carry out a supplier contingency test. What is the colleague?
why: A risk action owner is specifically assigned to perform an agreed response action.

stem: A possible positive event could reduce installation costs. The project funds a pilot to make the improvement more likely. What response is that?
why: Enhancement increases the likelihood or positive impact of an opportunity.

stem: A sponsor requests a different user interface after the approved product specification was baselined. What type of issue is this?
why: A proposed modification to the approved product baseline is a request for change.

stem: The impact of a logged change request on business case, risks and delivery scope needs to be understood. Which issue technique step is next?
why: Assess examines impact and severity after an issue has been captured.

stem: A component is now expected not to achieve an agreed technical specification, even though the team will still deliver it. What is the clearest issue type?
why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its agreed specification.

stem: The team manager predicts its work package will go over the agreed duration tolerance. Who should normally be informed first?
why: The project manager sets work-package tolerances and receives the team manager’s escalation.

stem: The project board requires a brief summary every two weeks about the stage being managed. Which report best supports this?
why: A highlight report is the project manager’s regular summary of stage progress to the board.

stem: A forecast shows that stage costs will exceed the tolerance granted by the board. What has occurred in PRINCE2 terms?
why: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond the relevant delegated tolerance.

stem: The project board must decide whether to invest in detailed initiation. Which process creates the early project brief and initiation stage plan?
why: Starting up a project tests viability cheaply, prepares the project brief and plans initiation.

stem: At the end of a management stage, updated business justification and a proposed plan for the next stage are needed. Who prepares these for board consideration?
option_A: Managing a stage boundary process led by the project manager
option_B: Directing a project process led by the team manager
option_C: Managing product delivery process led by the senior user
option_D: Closing a project process led by project support
correct_text: Managing a stage boundary process led by the project manager
why: The project manager uses managing a stage boundary to prepare end stage evidence, updated justification and the next plan.

stem: External conditions make continued delivery unjustified and the board orders the project stopped. What should happen to closure?
option_A: Skip closure because the work was not finished
option_B: The team manager issues a new project mandate
option_C: The board automatically transfers budget without reviewing products
option_D: Use the closing a project process to manage premature closure
correct_text: Use the closing a project process to manage premature closure
why: Closing a project also applies to premature closure to make responsibilities and incomplete work clear.

stem: A project combines detailed design followed by construction in a fixed sequence, but develops its customer portal in repeated small releases. Which term BEST describes its delivery approach?
why: Hybrid combines delivery approaches in one PRINCE2-governed project.

stem:
Which TWO statements describe the integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
1. People includes those working on and affected by the project.
2. Processes replace the need for practices.
3. Project context influences how the method is applied.
4. Practices are optional when a project is small.
why: Both 1 and 3 are true: people and context are among PRINCE2’s five integrated elements.

stem: A team begins defining detailed activities before agreeing which products meet user requirements. Which principle should it apply more carefully?
why: Focus on products means define the deliverables and their quality requirements before planning tasks in detail.

stem: A project manager suggests combining several management products into one digital record. Who is accountable for approving how PRINCE2 is tailored?
why: The project board is accountable for tailoring decisions; the project manager proposes the approach.

stem: Identify the missing words: PRINCE2 management by [?] permits decisions within delegated limits unless a forecast exceeds tolerance.
why: Management by exception uses tolerances to delegate decisions and escalate forecast breaches.

stem: A project team wants to replace PRINCE2 terminology with names already familiar across the organization. What should the project manager do?
option_A: Create a new principle for the revised terms
option_B: Drop the roles that have inconvenient names
option_C: Propose terminology changes for board approval and document the tailoring in the PID
option_D: Change the names without recording the decision
correct_text: Propose terminology changes for board approval and document the tailoring in the PID
why: Terminology can be tailored, with project-manager recommendation, board approval and PID documentation.

stem: A board authorizes only the next manageable portion of work after checking the updated business case. Which principle most directly describes this governance pattern?
why: Manage by stages allows planning and authorization at stage boundaries rather than committing all delivery detail at once.

stem:
Which TWO statements are consistent with the principle of continued business justification?
1. A project must begin with sufficient reason to invest.
2. A project continues automatically once delivery has started.
3. The justification is checked as circumstances change.
4. A finished output is proof that benefits have been realized.
why: 1 and 3 are true: the initial reason for investment must remain valid.

stem: A new scheduling system works correctly, but service managers refuse to use it. Which activity most directly supports the project’s intended benefits?
option_A: Issuing an exception plan solely because users have concerns
option_B: Planning how staff move to new working practices
option_D: Increasing system testing without asking users
correct_text: Planning how staff move to new working practices
why: Change management prepares the transition from current ways of working to the target organizational state.

stem: Two project teams have identical technical skills but achieve different results because trust and relationships differ. Which people concept does this BEST illustrate?
option_B: Project context is irrelevant when people are qualified
option_C: Relationships and team dynamics affect performance
correct_text: Relationships and team dynamics affect performance
why: PRINCE2 recognises that interactions, culture and relationships influence how effectively a team works.

stem: Identify the missing term: A person who can influence a project, is affected by it, or perceives an effect is a [?].
why: Stakeholder covers individuals, groups or organizations affecting or affected by the project, including perceived effects.

stem: A manager assigns tasks, checks that agreed procedures are followed and coordinates delivery. Which term best names this behaviour?
why: Management includes directing execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working.

stem: Users and key influencers jointly design the future customer-service process so that it will be adopted. What is this specifically called?
why: Co-creation is collaborative design with users and influencers that supports adoption.

stem: A communication approach schedules messages to stakeholders but has no process for stakeholders to respond. Which improvement best supports PRINCE2 7?
option_A: Replace it with a one-way progress newsletter
option_B: Escalate every comment to the project board
option_D: Communicate only when an exception occurs
why: The communication management approach should facilitate controlled, two-way information and feedback.

stem:
Which TWO statements about the project ecosystem are correct?
1. People affected by the project may sit outside its formal team.
2. All key influencers must be senior executives.
3. Supplier relationships may cross organizational boundaries.
4. Once the team is appointed, stakeholders never change.
why: 1 and 3 are true: project relationships extend beyond the formal team and may cross organizations.

stem: What is the principal purpose of the communication management approach?
option_A: Describe stakeholder information needs, channels, frequency and feedback
option_B: Specify who is permitted to approve changes to product baselines
option_C: Define the quality criteria for accepting the project product
option_D: Record all identified risk owners and their responses
correct_text: Describe stakeholder information needs, channels, frequency and feedback
why: Communication management defines how information is exchanged and feedback obtained across the project ecosystem.

stem: Which statement best distinguishes change management from change control in PRINCE2 7?
option_A: Change control manages staff training; change management logs defects
option_B: Change management prepares adoption of new ways of working; change control governs amendments to approved baselines
option_C: Both exclusively authorize revisions to baselined products
option_D: Neither term concerns users outside the project team
correct_text: Change management prepares adoption of new ways of working; change control governs amendments to approved baselines
why: The distinction is people adopting target-state working practices versus assessing and authorizing baseline changes.

stem: When developing a diverse hybrid team, which action is most consistent with the people guidance?
option_A: Use the same informal communication routine for everyone regardless of location
option_B: Assume identical abilities because job titles match
option_C: Identify capability gaps and build trust across locations and cultures
correct_text: Identify capability gaps and build trust across locations and cultures
why: Effective teams assess capabilities, diversity, cultural intelligence and ways to build cohesion.

stem: A council delivers new waste-sorting bins. Six months later, the percentage of material recycled rises measurably. Which item is the benefit?
why: The measurable improvement perceived as valuable is a benefit.

stem: The project manager updates forecast costs and risks in the business case after a supplier changes its price. Which business case technique step is most directly being performed?
why: Maintain keeps the business case current as costs, risks and forecasts change.

stem: At an end-stage decision the board asks whether the project remains desirable, viable and achievable. Which step of business case management is being applied?
why: Check assesses whether the business justification remains sound at decision points.

stem: Identify the missing word: A measurable adverse effect resulting from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization, is a [?].
why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline stemming from an outcome, not merely a possible future event.

stem: A project delivers its main product successfully, but realization of savings will take two years. What should happen to the scheduled benefits reviews?
option_A: The team manager keeps the project open indefinitely
option_B: The benefits are recorded as already achieved at handover
option_C: They cease as soon as the project closes
option_D: They continue in accordance with the benefits management approach under suitable business ownership
correct_text: They continue in accordance with the benefits management approach under suitable business ownership
why: The benefits management approach supports post-project reviews and assigned accountability for realization.

stem:
Which TWO statements about establishing business justification are correct?
1. The do-nothing option helps form an investment comparison.
2. All expected benefits must occur before a project can close.
3. Associated risks and dis-benefits can affect the choice.
4. The business case is unnecessary after initiation.
why: 1 and 3 are true: investment options must be compared considering risks and adverse effects.

stem: An organization wants the project to minimize its carbon footprint and sets measurable targets and review controls. Which management approach covers the actions for these targets?
why: Sustainability management approach defines actions, reviews and controls for achieving sustainability targets.

stem: The project board wants one individual ultimately accountable for the project’s business justification and funding. Which role is this?
why: The project executive is the single point of accountability for the investment and continuing business case.

stem: The executive is asked to appoint the same individual as the project manager because the project is small. What should happen?
option_A: Remove the executive if there is a project board
option_B: Give all accountability to project support
option_C: Combine both roles automatically because the project is small
option_D: Keep the project executive and project manager roles separate
correct_text: Keep the project executive and project manager roles separate
why: PRINCE2 does not allow the single accountable executive to be combined with the day-to-day project manager.

stem: A team manager is asked to deliver a work package within cost and time constraints. Who normally defines those work-package tolerances?
why: The project manager delegates work packages to teams and sets their tolerances.

stem: Which organizational level is OUTSIDE the project management team?
why: The business or commissioning layer sits above and outside the project management team.

stem:
Which TWO statements about project assurance are correct?
1. The board is accountable for ensuring its interests are assured.
2. Project assurance should always be performed by the project manager personally.
3. Assurance can be delegated to suitable people with sufficient independence.
4. Project support and assurance must be combined in one person.
why: 1 and 3 are true: the board retains assurance accountability and may arrange independent assurance.

stem: A work breakdown structure is used in the organization practice. What does it represent?
option_A: The levels of tolerance delegated by the board
option_B: Only the sequence of management stages
option_C: A register of known project issues
option_D: A hierarchy of the work required for the project
correct_text: A hierarchy of the work required for the project
why: The WBS is a hierarchical representation of all the work to be done, linking products to work packages.

stem: In organizational design and development, a completed product is handed over to the business team that will operate it. Which step is most directly involved?
option_A: Transition the project into organizational ecosystem
correct_text: Transition the project into organizational ecosystem
why: Transition ensures responsibilities and ways of working move into the operational ecosystem.

stem: A supplier needs to know precisely what products to deliver, their quality requirements, constraints and reporting duties. Which management product should be agreed?
why: A work package description records the agreement and constraints for team delivery.

stem: The project manager can accurately estimate the next six weeks but not the detailed work eighteen months away. What planning principle is most applicable?
option_A: Do not produce a high-level project plan
option_B: Delay defining all project products until the final stage
option_C: Use a planning horizon with detailed near-term stage plans
option_D: Plan the entire project at identical detail now
correct_text: Use a planning horizon with detailed near-term stage plans
why: The planning horizon uses detail appropriate to how far ahead the plan reaches, refining later stages nearer their start.

stem: Identify the missing words: A plan created in response to an exception to replace an existing plan is an [?].
why: An exception plan proposes revised work and control after a tolerance exception, subject to authorization.

stem: While constructing a product breakdown structure, the team realizes two products require a supplied component that the project itself will not create. How should this inform planning?
option_A: Recognize the external dependency and include it in planning assumptions and controls
option_B: Treat the product as automatically accepted
option_D: Ignore the external product because it is not created by the team
correct_text: Recognize the external dependency and include it in planning assumptions and controls
why: External dependencies influence estimates, delivery sequence and required control arrangements.

stem:
Which TWO statements about PRINCE2 plans are correct?
1. A project plan gives the overall view of the main products.
2. A team plan is mandatory for every work package.
3. A stage plan supports detailed control by the project manager.
4. Every exception plan must replace the entire business case.
why: 1 and 3 are true: the project plan is high-level and the stage plan is detailed.

stem: An activity cannot begin until a specialist item arrives from outside the project. What kind of dependency is this?
why: An external dependency relies on something outside the project’s direct control.

stem: Who normally uses a stage plan as the primary basis for managing a stage day to day?
why: The project manager uses the stage plan to coordinate and control stage work.

stem: Users will only accept the completed booking system if at least 95% of trial appointments can be booked without errors. What type of information is this?
why: An acceptance criterion defines a condition the overall project product must meet for user acceptance.

stem: An independent department reviews whether the project’s testing procedures comply with organizational standards, rather than testing the finished product. What function is illustrated?
why: Quality assurance gives planned independent confidence in the arrangements that enable product quality.

stem: The project manager wants to find all planned and completed inspections and their results. Which record is most directly useful?
why: The quality register records quality activities, their schedules and results.

stem:
Which TWO statements about quality are correct?
1. Quality assurance is typically managed independently of the project team.
2. A completed test automatically means the project product has been accepted.
3. Quality specifications state product measures and target levels.
4. User quality expectations should never be documented.
why: 1 and 3 are true: assurance is usually independent and specifications define measurable standards.

stem: A project needs to specify the methods, standards and responsibilities for performing quality checks. Which management product should be consulted?
why: The quality management approach explains quality techniques, standards, methods and responsibilities.

stem: Identify the missing phrase: The prioritized conditions that the overall project product must satisfy before the user accepts it are called [?].
why: Acceptance criteria are the conditions for acceptance of the project product as a whole.

stem: A storm could prevent construction next month. A storm did not occur yet. How should this normally be treated?
why: A risk is an uncertain future event whose occurrence would affect objectives.

stem: A possible new permit delay is likely to occur soon but would cause little disruption after occurrence. Which concepts distinguish these two assessments?
why: Proximity concerns how soon the event could occur; impact concerns the consequence for objectives.

stem: The business is willing to take very little uncertainty, and a proposed plan would exceed the defined acceptable exposure threshold. Which two terms distinguish the attitude from the measurable limit?
option_C: Risk action owner and risk budget
why: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is the measurable boundary for an objective at risk.

stem: A team is overconfident and ignores the possibility of failure because similar work usually goes well. Which decision-making problem is illustrated?
why: Optimism bias underestimates problems and overestimates the chance of favourable results.

stem:
Which TWO statements about risk response are correct?
1. Exploit is appropriate for some opportunities.
2. Avoid is the normal label for maximizing a positive opportunity.
3. Enhance may improve likelihood or impact of an opportunity.
4. All threats must be transferred to an insurer.
why: 1 and 3 are true: exploit and enhance are opportunity responses.

stem: During risk management, which activity should occur throughout the Identify–Assess–Plan–Implement technique?
option_B: Authorize every individual response at board level
why: Communication is carried out throughout risk management so relevant stakeholders understand threats and opportunities.

stem: The project manager receives a request to revise an already approved product specification. Which issue type applies?
why: A request for change is a proposal to modify the existing approved project baseline.

stem: A component will be delivered but will not meet its agreed weight limit. Which issue category fits?
why: Off-specification describes a product that will not meet its agreed specifications.

stem: The project manager evaluates how an issue could change cost, scope, benefits and the risk profile. Which issue-management step does that?
why: Assess investigates consequences and checks severity before recommendations or decisions.

stem: A change has been approved. The project manager arranges the corrective work and updates the relevant baseline and issue records. Which issue-management step is now being performed?
why: Implement carries out the authorised action and updates records and controlled products as needed.

stem:
Which TWO statements about project baselines are correct?
1. A baseline contains approved versions of relevant management and project products.
2. Any team member can change a baseline without authorization.
3. Changes to a baseline need the agreed control procedure.
4. Baselines become irrelevant as soon as an issue is raised.
why: 1 and 3 are true: baselines identify approved versions controlled through change procedures.

stem: The project board grants a delegated change authority permission to approve changes within an agreed limit. What is the main intended benefit?
option_B: Decisions can be made at an appropriate level without unnecessary escalation
option_C: All future changes become automatically approved
option_D: The board is no longer accountable for project performance
correct_text: Decisions can be made at an appropriate level without unnecessary escalation
why: Delegated authority supports timely decisions within limits while escalation remains available.

stem: The project manager must define how project information will be stored, secured, processed and used in reporting. Which PID component covers this?
why: The digital and data management approach explains how digital tools and data will be governed and used on the project.

stem: Actual progress data show a growing pattern of missed milestones even though the current stage is inside tolerance. What is the best use of the information?
option_A: Focus only on historic reporting because no limit is breached yet
option_B: Immediately issue an exception plan without any forecast breach
option_C: Stop collecting data until the stage boundary
option_D: Use the trend to forecast future stage performance and consider corrective action
correct_text: Use the trend to forecast future stage performance and consider corrective action
why: Trend information helps forecast whether future limits may be exceeded, enabling timely response.

stem: A team is slightly behind schedule but still forecasts completing within the agreed work-package tolerance. How should this normally be handled?
option_A: The team manager should manage the variance within authority and keep the project manager informed
option_C: Immediately escalate a stage exception to the board
option_D: Stop the project because the baseline cannot change
correct_text: The team manager should manage the variance within authority and keep the project manager informed
why: Management by exception permits local corrective action within tolerances, with routine reporting to the project manager.

stem: Identify the missing words: The management product that consolidates significant learning to share with future projects is the [?].
why: A lessons report captures conclusions and recommendations for others to use; it is distinct from the continuing log.

stem:
Which TWO statements about tolerances are correct?
1. The business layer normally sets project-level tolerances.
2. The project manager sets the project board’s stage-level tolerances.
3. The project board delegates stage tolerances to the project manager.
4. Every small variance automatically requires an exception report.
why: 1 and 3 are true: project tolerances come from the commissioning level and stage tolerances from the board.

stem: The board wants a report comparing overall project achievements against the original project baseline as part of closure. Which report is most appropriate?
why: The end project report compares project results with the original objectives and baselines to support closure.

stem: A project mandate has arrived, but the board wants to know if investing in detailed initiation is worthwhile. Which process should occur first?
why: Starting up a project checks whether there is a viable proposal before spending significant effort on initiation.

stem: A proposed project has only a mandate and an outline business case. Before the board authorizes full delivery, what additional foundation is normally required?
option_B: The detailed project initiation documentation prepared during initiating a project
option_D: An issue report closing every possible uncertainty
correct_text: The detailed project initiation documentation prepared during initiating a project
why: The PID and detailed business case provide the sound baseline and approaches for a delivery investment decision.

stem: The project manager needs to prepare a detailed business case, project management approaches and the project initiation documentation. Which process is responsible?
why: Initiating a project establishes the robust foundations and PID needed before authorizing delivery.

stem: During the initiation stage of a complex project, the project manager must coordinate work packages, track issues and report progress. Which process provides that day-to-day control?
why: Controlling a stage can apply to the initiation stage and coordinates day-to-day progress and work.

stem: A team agrees its work package, produces the requested products and hands them back for acceptance. Which process governs this team-level cycle?
why: Managing product delivery governs accepting, executing and delivering work packages.

stem: An end stage report and next stage plan are being prepared to support the board’s continuation decision. Which process produces these?
why: Managing a stage boundary prepares end-stage evidence, updates justification and proposes the next stage plan.

stem: A project is completing its final management stage. The users accept the products, but some follow-on operational action remains. What should the closing process do?
option_A: Keep the project permanently open until all possible operational improvements occur
option_C: Document follow-on action recommendations and arrange an orderly transfer to the appropriate owners
option_D: Skip the end project report because outstanding actions exist
correct_text: Document follow-on action recommendations and arrange an orderly transfer to the appropriate owners
why: Closing a project records unresolved matters and follow-on action recommendations while formal acceptance and handover are completed.

stem: The project board is reviewing a proposed next stage plan. In which process does the board make its authorization decision?
why: Directing a project contains the board’s decision to authorize a stage or provide direction.

stem:
Which TWO statements about project processes are correct?
1. The board authorizes initiation through directing a project.
2. Managing product delivery is exclusively a project board process.
3. Closing a project includes confirming product acceptance and handover.
4. Starting up a project is used after completing all delivery stages.
why: 1 and 3 are true: the board directs authorization and closing checks acceptance and handover.

stem: An exception is forecast during the final management stage. Can managing a stage boundary still be used to prepare an exception plan?
option_A: No, it is never used during the final stage
option_B: Yes, exception planning can be needed at any point, including the final stage
option_C: Only if the project is creating its initial project brief
option_D: No, all final-stage exceptions are automatically approved
correct_text: Yes, exception planning can be needed at any point, including the final stage
why: PRINCE2 notes that managing a stage boundary may be used to prepare an exception plan even in the final stage.

stem: Which process has the objective of ensuring that the project board can judge performance against agreed objectives and authorize its closure?
why: Closing a project confirms acceptance and handover, evaluates performance, and obtains closure authorization.

stem: The project manager is told a stage tolerance will be exceeded and asked to prepare a replacement plan. Which process prepares the exception plan for board consideration?
why: Managing a stage boundary also prepares exception plans when directed after a tolerance breach.

stem: A project manager consults five parts of PRINCE2: principles, people, practices, processes, and one more element. What is missing?
why: Project context is the fifth integrated element and affects how PRINCE2 is applied.

stem: A supplier joins a project and the team clarifies obligations, authority, reporting and relationships with users. Which principle is MOST directly involved?
why: This principle establishes a structure that engages business, user and supplier interests and clarifies relationships.

stem: The project manager finds that a previous project’s lessons log mentions difficult supplier handovers. What action best applies the associated principle?
option_A: Read the log only at the end of this project
option_B: Give all supplier decisions to the board
option_C: Adapt the current handover approach, record what works, and share the learning
option_D: Store the log but leave current plans unchanged
correct_text: Adapt the current handover approach, record what works, and share the learning
why: Learn from experience means seeking, applying and sharing lessons throughout delivery.

stem: Which statement BEST explains the relationship between the organizational ecosystem and the project ecosystem?
option_A: The organizational ecosystem contains only external suppliers
option_B: The project ecosystem includes only people formally paid by the project
option_C: The ecosystems must be completely separate to preserve governance
option_D: The project ecosystem interacts with the wider organizational ecosystem, including affected groups outside the formal team
correct_text: The project ecosystem interacts with the wider organizational ecosystem, including affected groups outside the formal team
why: Projects sit within wider organizations and interact with people who deliver, use and are affected by the work.

stem: A team member has the competence to complete a task but lacks access to the necessary specialist software. Which consideration should the project manager address?
option_A: Capability and practical resources needed to perform the role
option_C: The business case step called confirm
correct_text: Capability and practical resources needed to perform the role
why: Effective management considers capability, competence and whether assigned people can undertake the work.

stem: A project manager persuades different departments to support a difficult change by explaining the common objective and listening to concerns. This is an example of what?
why: Leadership motivates and influences stakeholders in pursuit of project objectives.

stem: What should a project change management approach describe?
option_A: The money authorized for unplanned baseline changes
option_B: A list of product quality test failures
option_C: How the organization will progress from its current state to the desired future state
option_D: Only the names of suppliers requesting changes
correct_text: How the organization will progress from its current state to the desired future state
why: Change management supports organizational transition, adoption and the target state needed for objectives.

stem:
Which TWO approaches help a hybrid project team maintain effective relationships?
1. Agree channels suited to remote and in-person participation.
2. Share information only with formally appointed team members.
3. Seek feedback from users affected by the change.
4. Assume all cultures prefer identical ways of collaborating.
why: 1 and 3 are correct: communication should fit hybrid work and include affected stakeholders.

stem: Which item normally provides the initial firm foundation on which the board decides whether to authorize project initiation?
option_A: Project brief with an outline justification
correct_text: Project brief with an outline justification
why: The project brief consolidates early project definition and outline business justification for authorizing initiation.

stem: The sponsoring business has a strategy to improve access to health services. How should a project benefit such as reduced waiting time be evaluated?
option_A: Only after any sustainability targets are removed
option_B: Against the business objective it is intended to contribute to
option_C: As equivalent to the physical equipment delivered
option_D: Only against the number of project team members
correct_text: Against the business objective it is intended to contribute to
why: Benefits should be measurable and show contribution to one or more business objectives.

stem: Which business case management step involves determining whether intended benefits have in fact been or will be realized?
why: Confirm considers benefit realization, often through post-project reviews.

stem: Who is responsible for maintaining sufficient ongoing commitment from people in the user community to adopt project products and realize benefits after closure?
why: The senior user represents the user community and supports adoption and continued benefits realization.

stem: A procurement-heavy project must document how supplier contracts and commercial arrangements will be managed. Where is this most appropriately covered?
why: The commercial management approach in the PID covers commercial arrangements for the project.

stem: The board delegates independent checks of business, user and supplier concerns to qualified colleagues. What remains true?
option_A: Assurance becomes unnecessary once a supplier delivers
option_B: The board remains accountable for ensuring adequate project assurance
option_C: The project manager takes over board accountability
option_D: Project support must sign off every check as final authority
correct_text: The board remains accountable for ensuring adequate project assurance
why: The board may delegate assurance activity while retaining accountability for its appropriate performance.

stem: A team manager would benefit from a short plan showing how to organize and control an assigned work package. What kind of plan is this?
why: A team plan is an optional plan to organize and control execution of a work package.

stem: A project plan allows the team to deliver 5% fewer product units than forecast without exceeding its approved scope constraint. What is this permissible variation called?
why: Scope tolerance defines the allowable variation in the products/deliverables included in a plan.

stem: A project manager determines the specialist equipment and staff effort needed to create products that have already been defined. Which part of planning is being performed?
why: Preparing estimates identifies needed resources, effort and cost based on products and work.

stem: A project manager wants the current approval state and version of each planned product. Which record helps most?
why: The product register maintains product status information, such as versions and approvals.

stem: What BEST distinguishes a product requirement from a quality specification?
option_A: They are interchangeable terms with no different purpose
option_B: A requirement exists only in the issue register
option_C: A requirement states a documented need; a quality specification describes how it will be measured and the required level
option_D: Specifications refer exclusively to benefits after project closure
correct_text: A requirement states a documented need; a quality specification describes how it will be measured and the required level
why: Requirements state documented needs or expectations; quality specifications set measurable quality criteria and levels.

stem: Which action supports accepting the overall project product rather than merely completing individual checks?
option_A: Treat any passing individual test as final user acceptance
option_C: Send a routine checkpoint report regardless of results
option_D: Apply agreed acceptance criteria and acceptance methods with the designated users
correct_text: Apply agreed acceptance criteria and acceptance methods with the designated users
why: Project product acceptance should follow the defined acceptance criteria, methods and authorized users.

stem: A supplier might fail, but another supplier will be held on standby and engaged only if failure occurs. What is this response?
why: A contingent plan identifies actions to take if the uncertain event occurs.

stem: Which wording correctly distinguishes cause, event and effect in a risk description?
option_A: All three describe the same thing
option_B: Cause creates conditions; event is what may happen; effect describes the consequence for objectives
option_C: Cause is the project board; event is the issue register; effect is the work package
option_D: Cause is the uncertainty; event is the financial benefit; effect is who owns the project
correct_text: Cause creates conditions; event is what may happen; effect describes the consequence for objectives
why: A useful risk statement connects the circumstances giving rise to the risk, the possible event and its effect on objectives.

stem: Decision-makers prefer the certainty of keeping an existing supplier even when evidence suggests a new supplier offers a better risk-adjusted result. Which bias may influence them?
why: Loss aversion can lead people to overweight giving up something they already have relative to a potential gain.

stem: A field-test failure has happened and requires an immediate repair; no approved scope revision is being proposed. Which issue class BEST fits?
why: A problem/concern is an event already affecting or requiring consideration by the project.

stem: A project has funds expressly reserved to cover authorized changes to product baselines. What are these funds called?
why: The change budget is money or authorized constraints set aside for approved changes.

stem: The board is assessing stage results and deciding whether to authorize the next stage. Which report summarizes the just-completed stage for that decision?
why: The end stage report summarizes stage performance and supports the board’s next-stage decision.

stem: Which approach to data best supports effective progress management?
option_A: Collecting only historic data with no forecast
option_B: Replacing board decisions with automatically generated metrics
option_C: Using accurate actuals and trends to forecast remaining work and emerging exceptions
option_D: Recording every item manually regardless of usefulness
correct_text: Using accurate actuals and trends to forecast remaining work and emerging exceptions
why: Good data and systems support timely forecasting and sound management decisions.

stem: At the start of a project, which process is responsible for preparing the initial project brief and initiation stage plan?
why: Starting up a project develops an early definition and plan to support initiation authorization.

stem:
Which TWO statements are correct at a management stage boundary?
1. The project manager prepares information for the board.
2. The team manager alone authorizes the next stage.
3. The business case is checked for continued justification.
4. A new project mandate must be created for every stage.
why: 1 and 3 are true: stage boundary planning and justification support the board’s stage authorization.

stem: The project manager prepares a draft closure notification and confirms outstanding matters have owners. Which process is being used?
why: Closing a project plans the controlled handover, notifications, lessons and recommendations for closure.

stem: The project manager and team manager agree on deliverables and constraints for a work package. Which two processes meet at this interface?
option_A: Directing a project and initiating a project
option_B: Starting up a project and closing a project
option_C: Controlling a stage and managing product delivery
option_D: Managing a stage boundary and closing a project
correct_text: Controlling a stage and managing product delivery
why: Controlling a stage authorizes and monitors work packages; managing product delivery accepts and executes them.

stem: Which project characteristic means a temporary team combines different specialist disciplines?
why: Correct. Cross-functional means bringing different skills and areas together to deliver change.

stem: A team designs products before a detailed activity schedule. Which principle drives this?
why: Correct. Focus on products defines deliverables and acceptance requirements before detailed activities.

stem: The system is delivered, but staff resist adopting a new workflow. Which management concern BEST addresses this?
option_A: Change management for the people affected
correct_text: Change management for the people affected
why: Correct. Change management considers stakeholder adoption and transition from the current to the target way of working.

stem: Which document should specify stakeholder communication needs, frequency and feedback arrangements?
why: Correct. The communication management approach sets out how information and feedback will flow across stakeholders.
