stem: Which statement BEST reflects leadership in a temporary project team?
option_B: Relationships, collaboration and different stakeholder motivations matter
option_C: All team members must be co-located
option_D: Project teams do not need feedback
correct_text: Relationships, collaboration and different stakeholder motivations matter
why: Correct. Relationships, collaboration, capability and motivation affect project performance.

stem: Which statement accurately distinguishes the two types of change discussed in PRINCE2 7?
option_A: People change management is the same as product baseline change control
option_B: Issue management handles changes to controlled baselines; change management addresses adoption by people
option_C: Only programme managers deal with staff adopting outputs
option_D: Change control is limited to risk events
correct_text: Issue management handles changes to controlled baselines; change management addresses adoption by people
why: Correct. Change management concerns people adopting new ways of working, while the Issues practice controls approved baseline changes.

stem: A new product is installed, staff begin using it, and order processing becomes faster. Which item is the benefit?
option_D: The decision to start the project
why: Correct. A measurable improvement from that outcome is a benefit.

stem: Which management product defines when project benefits will be reviewed, including after closure?
why: Correct. The benefits management approach sets arrangements for reviews, measurement and responsibilities over time.

stem: Who defines the tolerances within which the project board can direct the complete project?
why: Correct. The business layer sets project-level tolerances for the project board.

stem: A project manager also performs the team manager role on a small project. Which statement is correct?
option_B: Permissible if capability and capacity make this appropriate
option_C: Means the project manager also performs project assurance
correct_text: Permissible if capability and capacity make this appropriate
why: Correct. A project manager may also perform team management where sensible.

stem: What does a product breakdown structure show?
option_A: The hierarchy of products needed for the plan
option_B: The order and dependencies between product deliveries
option_C: The dates of every checkpoint report
correct_text: The hierarchy of products needed for the plan
why: Correct. The breakdown structure shows the product hierarchy and helps clarify scope.

stem: Which plan is optional and primarily helps the team manager control a work package?
why: Correct. A team plan may be prepared to organize and control team-level work packages.

stem: Who normally maintains details of planned quality activities and actual quality results?
why: Correct. A quality register records planned control activities and their outcomes.

stem: What distinguishes a project product description from an individual product description?
option_A: It defines overall acceptance of the project product
option_B: It is always created after project closure
option_D: It replaces the need for quality criteria
correct_text: It defines overall acceptance of the project product
why: Correct. The project product description defines the overall deliverable and acceptance criteria.

stem: A risk has a low chance of occurring but would affect objectives almost immediately after it happens. What characteristic is high?
why: Correct. Velocity is the speed with which the risk would affect objectives after occurrence.

stem: What is the best distinction between the risk owner and risk action owner?
option_A: Risk owner oversees the risk; risk action owner carries out allocated response actions
option_B: Risk owner manages the change budget; action owner signs the PID
option_C: Risk owner is always the executive; action owner always the senior user
option_D: Both roles only apply after an issue occurs
correct_text: Risk owner oversees the risk; risk action owner carries out allocated response actions
why: Correct. The risk owner retains responsibility for the risk while action owners implement agreed actions.

stem: Which phrase BEST describes risk proximity?
option_A: Likelihood that an event will occur
option_B: How near in time the event may occur
option_C: How quickly an effect will arise once the event occurs
option_D: The financial allowance for risk responses
correct_text: How near in time the event may occur
why: Correct. Proximity describes the nearness in time of possible occurrence.

stem: An approved requirement will not be met, and the project board agrees to accept the deviation without correction. What is this called?
why: Correct. A concession is acceptance of an off-specification without corrective action.

stem: Which practice manages a proposal to change an already approved product baseline?
why: Correct. The Issues practice includes the control of proposed baseline changes.

stem: Which of these is a time-driven management control?
option_A: Checkpoint report at an agreed weekly interval
option_C: Exception report after a forecast tolerance breach
correct_text: Checkpoint report at an agreed weekly interval
why: Correct. Repeating a checkpoint report at agreed intervals is time-driven.

stem: A team manager anticipates exceeding a work package tolerance. To whom should the issue first be raised?
why: Correct. The team manager raises the issue to the project manager for action within stage authority.

stem: Which report is produced periodically by the project manager for the project board?
why: Correct. Highlight reports provide periodic stage-level progress information to the board.

stem: What process prepares information for the board to approve a new delivery stage?
why: Correct. Stage boundary management prepares stage reports, next-stage plans and updated justification.

stem: Which process primarily manages acceptance, execution and delivery of a work package by a team?
why: Correct. Managing product delivery controls the team-manager interface for authorized work.

stem: An agency has run the same daily customer-support service for five years. Why is that not automatically a project?
option_A: It is continuing business-as-usual rather than a temporary organization created for change
option_C: It employs staff from several departments
correct_text: It is continuing business-as-usual rather than a temporary organization created for change
why: PRINCE2 projects are temporary and deliver a defined change; the ongoing service is operation.

stem: A new sustainability target is added to a project. Which statement about PRINCE2 7 performance is accurate?
option_A: Sustainability is one of seven aspects against which project performance can be controlled
option_B: Sustainability replaces quality as a performance aspect
option_C: Sustainability is only considered after project closure
option_D: Only financial metrics can have tolerances
correct_text: Sustainability is one of seven aspects against which project performance can be controlled
why: The seven aspects include benefits, costs, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk.

stem: Which combination correctly names the elements integrated in PRINCE2 7?
option_A: Principles, people, practices, processes, project context
option_B: Principles, themes, processes, products, project context
correct_text: Principles, people, practices, processes, project context
why: PRINCE2 7 integrates five elements: principles, people, practices, processes and context.

stem: A delivery team installs software in short iterations while the facilities work follows a fixed sequence. What describes the overall delivery approach?
why: Hybrid delivery combines iterative-incremental and linear-sequential ways of delivering products.

stem: A team says its project will never end because the new service will operate for years. What is the key misunderstanding?
option_A: The project can close when its products are accepted even while operations and benefits continue
option_B: A project may not close until every benefit is realized
option_C: A project ends the instant its business case is first approved
option_D: Any long-lived product makes the project permanent
correct_text: The project can close when its products are accepted even while operations and benefits continue
why: The project is temporary; the resulting service and post-project benefits may continue long afterward.

stem: Before committing to another stage, the board checks whether costs and anticipated benefits still justify continuing. Which principle is most directly visible?
why: The decision tests whether the project continues to be worthwhile for the business.

stem: A project manager retrieves a lessons report from a similar rollout before selecting a supplier. Which principle is illustrated?
why: Using relevant previous lessons before making decisions applies learn from experience.

stem: A project board authorizes the manager to spend within a cost range without asking for every minor decision. What makes this possible?
option_A: Manage by exception with delegated tolerances
option_B: Manage by stages with no delegated authority
option_C: Focus on products without quality criteria
option_D: Tailor away the approval process entirely
correct_text: Manage by exception with delegated tolerances
why: Tolerances define the manager’s decision boundary; forecast breaches are escalated.

stem: A small internal project decides not to define who represents users. Which statement is correct?
option_A: The method should be tailored, but user interests and responsibilities still need clear representation
option_B: This is acceptable because the project is small
option_C: The project manager automatically replaces every project board role
option_D: Small projects do not have to justify their investment
correct_text: The method should be tailored, but user interests and responsibilities still need clear representation
why: The PRINCE2 principles still apply, including defined roles, responsibilities and relationships.

stem: The team defines the acceptance criteria before building a new customer portal. Which principle is the strongest match?
why: Clear product expectations and quality criteria come before detailed activities.

stem: Which statement describes appropriate tailoring of PRINCE2 7?
option_A: Terminology and detail can be adapted while every principle still applies
option_B: A riskier project may discard the risk practice
option_C: The executive alone may remove principles to reduce paperwork
option_D: Tailoring is performed only after the project has closed
correct_text: Terminology and detail can be adapted while every principle still applies
why: Tailoring fits the method to the context without discarding its principles.

stem: Users fear that a new system will change their daily tasks. Which action best addresses the people element?
option_A: Engage affected people and plan the transition to new ways of working
option_B: Treat all resistance as an off-specification
option_C: Wait for final acceptance before discussing the change
option_D: Ask only the technical supplier to define user adoption
correct_text: Engage affected people and plan the transition to new ways of working
why: People and organizational change require engagement, support and feedback throughout delivery.

stem: A team holds workshops where operational users shape the proposed solution. What is this best described as?
why: Co-creation invites those affected by the change to help shape what is delivered.

stem: Which information belongs primarily in the communication management approach?
option_A: Who needs information, the channels, frequency and feedback arrangements
option_B: The detailed quality criteria for a specialist product
option_C: The current status of each issue in the issue register
option_D: The board’s decision on a particular exception report
correct_text: Who needs information, the channels, frequency and feedback arrangements
why: The approach defines how two-way communication with stakeholders is managed.

stem: An employee outside the project team says the outcome will disrupt their job. Are they a stakeholder?
option_A: Yes, because a stakeholder may be affected without holding a project role
option_B: No, only members of the project board are stakeholders
option_C: Only if they approve the business case
option_D: Only if they work for an external supplier
correct_text: Yes, because a stakeholder may be affected without holding a project role
why: Stakeholders can affect or be affected by the project, including people outside the management team.

stem: A temporary cross-organization team is struggling with trust and different working cultures. What should its leader do?
option_A: Build shared ways of working and support team cohesion
option_B: Ignore the differences because relationships are not examinable
option_C: Delegate all culture problems to the risk owner
option_D: Remove user representatives to reduce debate
correct_text: Build shared ways of working and support team cohesion
why: Leading successful teams includes cultural awareness, collaboration and social cohesion.

stem: Which distinction is most helpful when reading a scenario about organizational adoption?
option_A: Change management helps people transition; issue/change control governs modifications to baselines
option_B: Change management and issue control are identical
option_C: A request for change always means users dislike the new system
option_D: The project should ignore stakeholder feedback until after closure
correct_text: Change management helps people transition; issue/change control governs modifications to baselines
why: People-focused change management differs from control of requests to modify approved baselines.

stem: A project delivers new booking software, and customers then begin booking online. What is the customers’ new behaviour?
why: The new pattern of behaviour enabled by the product is an outcome.

stem: Online bookings reduce call-centre costs by €30,000 annually. What is that quantified improvement?
why: A measurable improvement resulting from an outcome is a benefit.

stem: A new self-service portal saves money but increases accessibility complaints. What is the increase in complaints?
why: A measurable negative consequence of the change may be recorded as a dis-benefit.

stem: Who has ultimate accountability for the business case and the investment justification?
why: The executive represents the business interest and is accountable for the business case.

stem: Which management product describes how and when expected benefits will be measured?
why: The benefits management approach sets benefit review actions, responsibilities and timing.

stem: The project board checks the business case before approving a new delivery stage. Why?
option_A: To confirm that continuing the project still makes sense
option_B: To replace the independent assurance function
option_C: To prove every benefit has already been realized
option_D: To approve every individual work package
correct_text: To confirm that continuing the project still makes sense
why: Investment justification must be maintained and reviewed during project life.

stem: A team is selecting between two alternative ways to deliver the same outcomes. Which practice primarily establishes the investment case for the preferred option?
why: The business case evaluates business options and whether the preferred approach is worth investing in.

stem: The board has delegated delivery work to the project manager. Which person normally agrees the work package directly with the manager?
why: The team manager accepts and delivers agreed work packages from the project manager.

stem: A specialist lead forecasts that an agreed work package will exceed its time tolerance. Who should receive the escalation?
why: The team manager raises the work-package issue to the project manager for decision.

stem: Who represents the supplier perspective and is accountable for technical integrity?
why: The senior supplier represents delivery expertise and supplier resources and quality.

stem: Why must project assurance remain separate from the project manager?
option_A: To preserve independent assessment on behalf of the project board
option_B: Because assurance approves every team plan
option_D: Because assurance sets all project-level tolerances
correct_text: To preserve independent assessment on behalf of the project board
why: The project board must be assured independently of the person managing the work.

stem: A small project’s manager also directly leads the specialist team. Is this always forbidden?
option_A: No, the project manager may also perform the team manager role when appropriate
option_B: Yes, all PRINCE2 roles must be held by different people
option_C: Yes, because the project manager must also be the executive
option_D: No, because the board no longer needs to exist
correct_text: No, the project manager may also perform the team manager role when appropriate
why: PRINCE2 allows some roles to be combined; managing and delivering may be combined with suitable skills.

stem: Who establishes the project-level tolerances within which the project board operates?
why: The organization/business layer commissions the project and sets its overall tolerances.

stem: The board delegates authority to decide certain changes up to an agreed budget. What role is receiving that authority?
why: A change authority may approve specified change decisions within delegated limits.

stem: The board wants to understand the main products, schedule and budget for the entire project. Which plan is primarily relevant?
why: The project plan outlines the overall delivery and major targets across the project.

stem: A project manager needs sufficiently detailed control information for the next management stage. What should be prepared?
why: The stage plan provides the basis for detailed day-to-day stage management.

stem: The team leader needs to schedule the tasks for their assigned work package. Which plan may be useful?
why: Team plans are optional but support organizing and controlling a team’s work package.

stem: Which statement best describes an exception plan?
option_A: It is prepared to replace a plan when the relevant authority requests a response to an exception
option_B: It is the mandatory first plan written for a project
option_C: It describes how to communicate with stakeholders
option_D: It records the results of every quality check
correct_text: It is prepared to replace a plan when the relevant authority requests a response to an exception
why: An exception plan may replace a project or stage plan following an exception decision.

stem: Which action comes first in product-based planning?
option_A: Define and analyse the required products
option_B: Assign every specialist activity a person before defining products
correct_text: Define and analyse the required products
why: Product-based planning starts with understanding the outputs and their interdependencies.

stem: A project team asks what shows the hierarchy of products required by a plan. Which technique output provides that?
why: A product breakdown structure groups products in a hierarchy.

stem: A diagram shows that the test environment must exist before the application can be validated. What does it illustrate?
why: A product flow diagram highlights which products are needed before others.

stem: A product description lists the tests a new data extract must pass. What are those tests?
why: Product descriptions specify expected quality and how it is checked.

stem: A product is delivered but fails its agreed acceptance criterion. What should the team do?
option_A: Record the quality result and resolve the nonconformance through the appropriate control arrangements
option_B: Mark the product accepted because it was delivered on schedule
option_C: Move the failure into the benefits management approach
option_D: Stop quality checking all other products
correct_text: Record the quality result and resolve the nonconformance through the appropriate control arrangements
why: Quality checks establish whether products meet their specifications; failed criteria require action.

stem: What is the difference between quality assurance and project assurance?
option_A: Quality assurance is typically independent of the project; project assurance represents board interests within project governance
option_B: Project assurance is the same as the team’s quality test
option_C: Quality assurance always reports directly to the team manager
option_D: Neither should be independent of the project manager
correct_text: Quality assurance is typically independent of the project; project assurance represents board interests within project governance
why: Organizational quality assurance and project board assurance are related but different functions.

stem: Where would you expect to find scheduled and completed quality checks for project products?
why: The quality register tracks quality activities and their results.

stem: Which statement about acceptance criteria is most accurate?
option_A: They describe what the overall project product must satisfy to be accepted
option_B: They are the same as work-package cost tolerances
option_C: They are used only when the project has closed prematurely
option_D: They replace all individual product quality specifications
correct_text: They describe what the overall project product must satisfy to be accepted
why: Acceptance criteria define the conditions for customer/user acceptance of the project product.

stem: A requirement changes after a product has been approved as the baseline. Which practice deals with the request for modification?
why: The Issues practice controls requests to alter approved baselines, even if discovered during quality work.

stem: A team begins writing a solution without agreeing what “fit for purpose” means. What is the key risk?
option_A: Quality expectations and criteria are not yet agreed
option_B: The board has used too many management stages
option_C: Every risk is automatically an issue
correct_text: Quality expectations and criteria are not yet agreed
why: Quality planning requires a clear specification of what success looks like before verification.

stem: A port strike has not happened, but it could delay equipment delivery. How should the possibility be classified?
option_C: A confirmed issue with no uncertainty
why: An uncertain future event that could harm objectives is a threat risk.

stem: A risk is expected to occur around the final delivery week. Which attribute describes its position in time?
why: Proximity describes when a risk might occur.

stem: A cyber incident could disrupt operations within minutes if it occurs. Which risk attribute is described by the rapid onset of effects?
why: Velocity is the speed with which the impact follows the risk event.

stem: Which person is accountable for monitoring and controlling an assigned uncertainty over time?
why: The risk owner is accountable for the risk and its overall response.

stem: A mitigation task is assigned to the network engineer while the operations lead retains accountability for the overall risk. Who is the engineer?
option_B: The executive solely because there is a budget
why: The risk action owner carries out nominated response tasks.

stem: A favorable exchange rate might lower procurement costs. Which response aims to make that upside more likely or greater?
why: Enhance increases the probability or benefit of an opportunity.

stem: Which sequence is consistent with the PRINCE2 7 risk-management technique?
option_A: Identify, assess, plan, implement, with communication throughout
option_C: Only log risks after they have happened
option_D: Start with an exception report for every possible risk
correct_text: Identify, assess, plan, implement, with communication throughout
why: Risk management cycles through identifying, assessing, planning and implementing, with communication.

stem: A customer requests an additional reporting feature after the agreed product baseline has been approved. What type of issue is this?
why: A proposal to alter an approved baseline is a request for change.

stem: Tests show that a delivered component will not meet its quality specification. Which issue label fits?
why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its approved quality specifications.

stem: The team reports a minor day-to-day concern that the manager can resolve informally. Where can it initially be recorded?
why: Informal issues can be captured in the daily log within the project log.

stem: A proposed baseline change is beyond the manager’s delegated change authority. Who needs to make the approval decision?
option_A: The project board or the authority to which that decision has properly been delegated
option_C: Any team member who identifies it
option_D: The senior supplier acting alone in every case
correct_text: The project board or the authority to which that decision has properly been delegated
why: Change decisions must follow agreed delegated authority limits, ultimately under the project board.

stem: Which sequence best describes the main issue-management decision cycle?
option_B: Plan, direct, close, then define the issue
option_C: Record only, because all issues resolve themselves
option_D: Approve first and analyse after delivery
why: The issue-management technique captures and assesses an issue before recommending, deciding and implementing a response.

stem: A quality defect is accepted without correction by an authorized decision-maker. What is this acceptance called?
why: A concession is a decision to accept an off-specification without corrective action.

stem: A team manager sends its weekly status to the project manager. Which management report is most likely?
why: A checkpoint report summarizes work-package progress from delivering to managing level.

stem: Every month the project manager updates the board on stage progress. What report is this?
why: Highlight reports provide periodic progress information from the project manager to the board.

stem: A work package will exceed its agreed effort limit, but the stage can still remain within its own tolerance. What should happen first?
option_A: The team manager raises an issue to the project manager for a decision
option_B: The team manager sends an exception report directly to business management
option_C: The board must automatically close the project
option_D: The team quietly adjusts the approved work package baseline
correct_text: The team manager raises an issue to the project manager for a decision
why: The team escalates a forecast work-package deviation to the project manager, who can decide within stage authority.

stem: The current stage is forecast to exceed its authorized cost tolerance. What is the project manager expected to produce?
option_A: An exception report to the project board
option_C: A revised baseline without telling the board
correct_text: An exception report to the project board
why: A forecast stage-level tolerance breach is escalated through an exception report.

stem: Which type of control is a planned weekly checkpoint report?
why: A report scheduled at regular calendar intervals is time-driven.

stem: Which of these is an event-driven control?
option_A: A review at the end of a management stage
correct_text: A review at the end of a management stage
why: A stage-end authorization point is triggered by a milestone/event rather than a calendar frequency.

stem: An exception plan is approved to replace the current stage plan. Who approves that replacement?
why: The project board directs how a stage-level exception is resolved and approves the replacement plan.

stem: The project mandate has arrived, but detailed investment has not been authorized. What process checks that a worthwhile project can be initiated?
why: Starting up a project tests the prerequisites and develops an initial brief before initiation authorization.

stem: A project board must decide whether to fund initiation and later whether to authorize delivery. What overarching process covers its decisions?
why: Directing a project provides board-level authorization and decisions throughout the lifecycle.

stem: The manager prepares the detailed business case, project plan and management approaches before major commitment. Which process?
why: Initiating establishes the sound delivery and governance baseline presented through the PID.

stem: The manager authorizes work packages, monitors issues and sends regular progress to the board. Which process is in use?
why: Controlling a stage covers assigning work, tracking progress and corrective action inside a stage.

stem: A team manager accepts agreed work, creates products and returns completed packages. Which process governs that relationship?
why: Managing product delivery formalizes agreement, execution and handback of work packages.

stem: An end-stage report and next stage plan are prepared for a board decision. Which process provides this material?
why: The manager uses managing a stage boundary to review performance and seek next-stage approval.

stem: The project product is accepted and operations has taken responsibility for support. Which process confirms project completion?
why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, handover, performance and remaining follow-up actions.

stem: The project is stopped early because the business case is no longer justified. What should still happen?
option_A: Orderly premature closure, including handover and unresolved-action arrangements
option_B: No closure process because the original products are incomplete
option_C: Automatic approval of all incomplete deliverables
option_D: Erase all issue and risk records
correct_text: Orderly premature closure, including handover and unresolved-action arrangements
why: PRINCE2 supports controlled premature closure rather than abandoning the project.

stem: The project board receives an exception report and asks for a replacement stage plan. Which process prepares that plan for review?
why: Managing a stage boundary may prepare an exception plan for board consideration.

stem: Which process normally spans most of the project life because the board keeps giving direction at key points?
why: Directing provides overall board control and key authorizations across the project lifecycle.

stem: A council delivers a one-off replacement of its permit system, then returns to normal operations. What makes this work a project?
option_D: It is temporary and introduces a change through defined products
correct_text: It is temporary and introduces a change through defined products
why: The finite organization and intended change are project characteristics, unlike a permanent operational service.

stem: A construction team completes foundations, then walls, then roofing, with each phase depending on completion of the previous one. Which delivery approach does this describe?
why: A linear-sequential approach creates products in a largely fixed order, using earlier outputs before later work begins.

stem: A flood-defence project builds barriers in a fixed order while releasing its resident-alert app through several feedback-led increments. What delivery approach fits the project?
why: Hybrid delivery combines sequential construction with iterative-incremental software releases within one project.

stem: An organization wants to use PRINCE2 for a small charity event and a multinational construction programme. Which characteristic of PRINCE2 supports both?
option_A: The seven principles are optional for small projects
option_C: The method is tailored to the project context
option_D: Every management product must be a separate long document
correct_text: The method is tailored to the project context
why: PRINCE2 can be adapted to scale, complexity, commercial context, delivery approach and capabilities.

stem: A board discovers that a technically successful project no longer delivers value for money. Which principle should govern the next decision?
why: A project must remain worthwhile throughout its life, not merely be technically achievable.

stem: The initiation team reviews the risks and successes of a similar project and changes its approach. Which principle is most directly demonstrated?
why: Using relevant prior lessons to improve the current project is a direct application of learning from experience.

stem: The project board agrees that the senior user will represent beneficiaries and the senior supplier will represent technical delivery. Which principle is illustrated?
why: This principle ensures business, user and supplier interests have clear representation and decision rights.

stem: The project board approves only the next three months of detailed delivery, leaving later work at high level. Which principle is most evident?
why: PRINCE2 authorizes and controls work one management stage at a time, with appropriate detail for the near term.

stem: The project manager can spend up to an agreed limit without asking the board, but must escalate a forecast breach. Which principle allows this?
why: Agreed tolerances define how much authority is delegated and when escalation becomes necessary.

stem: A software project lists all outputs with measurable acceptance criteria before producing a detailed activity schedule. Which principle is foremost?
why: The team first defines what is to be delivered and accepted before deciding how to perform the work.

stem: A tiny project combines two reporting documents into one concise document. What is the correct statement?
option_A: The project must copy every template exactly
option_B: Combining management products may be a valid tailoring choice if required information is retained
option_C: The project may omit manage by exception if it is small
option_D: The team can ignore the project board once the documents are combined
correct_text: Combining management products may be a valid tailoring choice if required information is retained
why: Tailoring can simplify documentation to suit the project while preserving necessary governance information.

stem: Which statement about tailoring to project conditions is correct?
option_A: Tailoring can only take place after closing a project
option_B: Tailoring concerns only which software tools are used
option_C: The application of PRINCE2 can be adjusted, but all principles remain applicable
option_D: Principles are optional if the project has fewer than ten people
correct_text: The application of PRINCE2 can be adjusted, but all principles remain applicable
why: The method is adapted to the context; removing a principle would stop it being a genuinely PRINCE2-managed project.

stem: A project manager is asked to ignore a forecast tolerance breach until the next scheduled highlight report. Which principle is at risk?
why: Forecast exceptions must be escalated promptly to the authority that set the tolerance; routine reporting does not replace escalation.

stem: A sponsor says that because requirements are fixed, the project need not review whether the business case remains sound. What is the best response?
option_A: Business justification must continue to be assessed even if product scope remains unchanged
option_B: Fixed scope proves the project remains desirable
option_C: The business case need only be checked after closure
option_D: The senior supplier can replace the business case with a quality checklist
correct_text: Business justification must continue to be assessed even if product scope remains unchanged
why: Economic and organizational circumstances can change independently of the approved product scope.

stem: A new team has uncertainty about priorities. The project manager sets clear objectives, responsibilities and working rules. What is this principally?
why: Management establishes work arrangements, objectives and control so that coordinated delivery can occur.

stem: A team is losing motivation during an organizational transition. A leader influences, listens and inspires a shared purpose. Which concept is central?
why: Leadership motivates and influences people and builds commitment, particularly where direct authority is limited.

stem: An employee affected by a new payroll system has no formal project role. How should the project treat this person?
option_A: As a project board member automatically
option_B: As someone outside the scope of communication
option_C: As a supplier simply because they use software
option_D: As a stakeholder whose needs and feedback may matter
correct_text: As a stakeholder whose needs and feedback may matter
why: Stakeholders include people affected by a project, whether or not they hold a position in its governance structure.

stem: A public-sector project has an internal project team and external residents impacted by its outcome. Which distinction matters?
option_A: People delivering the project and people affected by it may both require engagement
option_B: Only employees with project roles count as stakeholders
option_C: Only senior managers may influence adoption
option_D: Every affected person must be made a project manager
correct_text: People delivering the project and people affected by it may both require engagement
why: PRINCE2 people guidance covers those working on change and those who experience its consequences.

stem: A project communicates its timetable to users but never asks whether it will disrupt essential services. What is missing?
why: Effective engagement involves gathering reactions and feedback, not only sending one-way announcements.

stem: Which management product should describe how information is shared with stakeholders and feedback is received?
why: The communication management approach defines the intended communication methods, timing, roles and feedback flows.

stem: A hospital team needs a plan for changing staff routines as a new clinical system goes live. Which management product is most relevant?
why: The change management approach describes how affected people move from current to future ways of working.

stem: Two departments jointly design a new customer journey, creating the solution together rather than handing off completed specifications. Which people concept is best illustrated?
why: Co-creation involves people jointly shaping outcomes and producing value, rather than simply passing completed work between groups.

stem: Staff from different organizations work together on a shared plan while retaining separate responsibilities. What concept is being applied?
why: Collaboration means working together towards agreed project goals, even where responsibilities remain distinct.

stem: The delivery organization has a strong blame culture, and staff hide bad news about delays. Which people factor should be addressed?
why: A blame culture discourages openness; effective leadership should support trust, honest information and safe escalation.

stem: A project includes specialists with the right technical skills but no experience of the chosen delivery method. What should be considered?
option_A: Replacing all experienced staff with new hires
why: An effective team needs appropriate capabilities and competence; gaps should be understood and addressed.

stem: A team works across three time zones. What should influence how it communicates?
option_A: Working arrangements and accessible communication channels
option_C: The fixed physical location of the project board
option_D: The total number of outputs in the project plan
correct_text: Working arrangements and accessible communication channels
why: Communication methods should accommodate remote, hybrid and geographically dispersed contributors.

stem: A new trade union representative becomes important because the project affects working patterns. What should the project team do?
option_A: Remove all existing users from the stakeholder list
option_B: Review stakeholder engagement and communication arrangements
option_C: Wait until closing a project to communicate
option_D: Automatically appoint the representative as executive
correct_text: Review stakeholder engagement and communication arrangements
why: Relevant stakeholders and their influence can change during the lifecycle, so engagement plans should be reviewed.

stem: An external charity can influence whether the intended project benefits are accepted, even without a project role. What is it?
why: A stakeholder may affect, be affected by or consider itself affected by the project; formal appointment is not required.

stem: A manager sends a detailed report but fails to learn that community groups cannot understand its technical language. What communication improvement is best?
option_A: Send the same report more often
option_C: Delegate the entire communication function to the supplier
option_D: Adapt content to the audience and seek feedback
correct_text: Adapt content to the audience and seek feedback
why: Effective communication considers different audiences and verifies that messages are understood.

stem: An organization asks how the project will support adoption after installing a new service. Which concern is central to change management?
option_A: Helping people transition from current working practices to the target state
option_D: Replacing the business case with a work package
correct_text: Helping people transition from current working practices to the target state
why: A new product alone does not ensure people adopt changed routines and realize intended outcomes.

stem: A temporary team includes people from different professional and cultural backgrounds. What approach is most consistent with the people element?
option_A: Allow only project board members to propose improvements
option_B: Value diverse perspectives and agree effective ways of working together
option_C: Assume everyone uses the same communication style
option_D: Exclude stakeholders outside the project organization
correct_text: Value diverse perspectives and agree effective ways of working together
why: Teams benefit from cultural awareness, inclusion, clarity and trust in cross-functional collaboration.

stem: A new digital service is completed and available to customers. What does its availability represent before anyone changes their behaviour?
why: The service is a deliverable produced by project activity; outcomes arise when people use it differently.

stem: After a new scheduling tool is introduced, staff stop manually allocating appointments. Which term best describes the changed working practice?
why: The changed way staff work is a result of using the product, so it is an outcome.

stem: A new system reduces the average claims-processing time from 12 days to 7 days. What is the five-day reduction?
why: The measurable improvement from the changed service is a benefit attributable to the outcome.

stem: A new transport system improves journey times but creates extra noise for nearby residents. How should the expected noise impact be described?
why: A dis-benefit is an anticipated measurable adverse result of an outcome, considered in business justification.

stem: A university plans to measure staff time saved by a new admissions system 18 months after project closure. Which management product should assign the ownership and timing of that review?
why: This approach specifies benefit measurement actions, reviews, ownership and timings, including relevant post-project reviews.

stem: A sustainability performance target must be monitored during delivery. Which management product explains how such targets will be managed?
why: This approach defines management actions and controls for meeting agreed sustainability performance targets.

stem: Before agreeing substantial investment, the board asks for more detailed costs, benefits, options and risks than were available during start-up. Which product should have been developed further?
why: The outline justification is developed into a fuller business case to support authorization of significant project investment.

stem: In the business case management technique, a review finds costs have doubled. What is the purpose of checking the justification?
option_A: To eliminate the need to update forecasts
option_B: To determine whether the investment remains worthwhile
option_C: To guarantee that all forecast benefits have already occurred
option_D: To authorize a team plan without project board control
correct_text: To determine whether the investment remains worthwhile
why: Checking tests continued desirability, viability and achievability in light of current estimates and assumptions.

stem: Which TWO statements are correct about business justification? 1. Expected dis-benefits can affect an investment decision. 2. Project justification is only documented after closure. 3. The executive is accountable for the business case. 4. The team manager owns the business case.
why: Statements 1 and 3 are true: adverse consequences are part of the investment picture and the executive owns business justification.

stem: A sponsor claims the project must stay open until every benefits target has been fully demonstrated. What is the most accurate correction?
option_A: The project manager must keep the project open forever
option_B: Only suppliers are responsible for realizing business benefits
option_C: Benefit forecasts should be discarded as soon as a product is accepted
option_D: Some benefits may need to be measured after project closure
correct_text: Some benefits may need to be measured after project closure
why: The benefits management approach can arrange follow-up reviews in operations when benefits take time to appear.

stem: A business needs one person to carry ultimate project accountability and own the business case. Who should fill this role?
why: The executive represents the business interest, owns the business case and is the single point of accountability.

stem: A museum needs someone to safeguard the needs of visitors and ensure its new exhibition delivers intended user benefits. Which board role?
why: The senior user represents user needs and the approach to realizing intended benefits.

stem: A supplier team is uncertain whether specialist engineers will be available to build a product to specification. Which board interest should ensure that capability?
why: The senior supplier represents delivery expertise, supplier resources and technical integrity.

stem: A parent organization sets the total project cost and time tolerance before the project board starts directing work. Which management layer does this?
why: The commissioning business layer sets overall requirements and project-level tolerance boundaries for the board.

stem: A project board authorizes a stage and delegates the day-to-day control of its delivery. Who receives that authority?
why: The project manager runs the project day to day within limits delegated by the project board.

stem: Why must project assurance remain independent from the project manager?
option_A: Because quality assurance and project assurance are identical
option_B: So the board receives an objective view of the project and its management
option_C: Because project assurance has authority to approve all team plans
option_D: Because the project manager must not receive any advice
correct_text: So the board receives an objective view of the project and its management
why: Assurance safeguards business, user and supplier interests without being controlled by the person it is assessing.

stem: A specialist team needs meeting coordination, document tracking and help using the project management tools. Which role typically provides this?
why: Project support provides administrative, coordination and technical support services to project management.

stem: A project manager agrees a work package with a team manager. Who controls the specialists performing that package?
why: The team manager organizes and delivers the agreed work package within the delegated constraints.

stem: A project manager must decide how project work packages map to specialist teams. Which structure is especially useful?
why: A work breakdown structure divides the effort and helps identify team boundaries and work package responsibilities.

stem: The project involves several suppliers with different contract obligations. Which approach should clarify how the commercial relationships will be managed?
why: The commercial management approach covers relationships and controls for supplier and contractual arrangements.

stem: A board member needs a high-level view of the main products, overall costs and key milestones from initiation through closure. What should they review?
why: The project plan gives an overall view of the major deliverables, timetable and resources across the project.

stem: An approved management stage is about to begin. The project manager needs product delivery dates, detailed costs and work assignments for everyday control. Which baseline should be used?
why: A stage plan provides the level of detail needed for day-to-day stage management and control.

stem: A specialist delivery lead wants to organize internal activities and resources for a work package. What plan may be useful?
why: A team plan is an optional way for a team manager to schedule and control team work.

stem: The board requests a new plan to replace the current stage plan after an exception. What kind of plan is required?
why: An exception plan is prepared to replace the plan that is no longer achievable once an exception decision requires replanning.

stem: The project manager needs to agree the products, interfaces, constraints and reporting for one team assignment. Which management product is most appropriate?
why: A work package description formalizes the delegated work and how it will be accepted, reported and delivered.

stem: The team needs the overall project's acceptance methods, customer quality expectations and acceptance criteria before defining specialist products. Where should it look?
why: This description specifies the overall project product and requirements for acceptance.

stem: Which output of defining and analysing products shows products grouped in a hierarchy, rather than their delivery order?
why: A product breakdown structure depicts the products to be delivered as a hierarchy.

stem: A plan shows that training materials cannot be finalized until a new process is approved. What is the relationship called?
why: A dependency means work on one product or activity relies on another being completed or available.

stem: Why might detailed plans for work eighteen months away be less reliable than for the next eight weeks?
option_A: Every future stage must begin immediately
option_B: Technical teams should never estimate costs
option_C: The planning horizon makes near-term estimates more dependable
option_D: PRINCE2 forbids a high-level project plan for the whole project
correct_text: The planning horizon makes near-term estimates more dependable
why: Progressively detailed planning uses the higher certainty available nearer the point of delivery.

stem: Which TWO statements about planning are correct? 1. The project plan identifies major products and overall delivery. 2. An exception plan is a compulsory extra planning level on every project. 3. Team plans must be approved personally by the project board. 4. Plans support communication and control.
why: Statement 1 is true because the project plan covers overall delivery; statement 4 is true because plans communicate and control the work.

stem: The project has defined a limit of 0.5% defects for an individual software product. Where should the product-specific test requirement be defined?
why: A product description includes quality specifications, quality methods and criteria for checking the product.

stem: A user says a new reception area should feel welcoming. What is that statement most likely to be before detailed measurable criteria are agreed?
why: User quality expectations capture the desired qualities at a high level before they are translated into measurable criteria.

stem: A museum states that a new booking system must process a payment in less than three seconds. What does this define?
why: The maximum processing time is a testable standard for the product's required performance.

stem: A project manager wants to see planned inspections and which product checks have been performed. Which record should they open?
why: The quality register records scheduled quality activities and their completion or results.

stem: Which management product best answers: which project products exist and what is each one's current status?
why: The product register provides control information about products and their current states across the project.

stem: A developer tests an interface against the specified response time before it is released. Which activity is this?
why: Quality control verifies specific products through inspections, tests and reviews against their requirements.

stem: An external company audits the project's compliance with the organization's quality framework independently of the project team. What is this?
why: Independent assurance checks the adequacy and application of quality arrangements and organizational standards.

stem: The organization wants a document specifying quality techniques, standards and responsibilities to be used throughout the project. Which management product fits?
why: This approach explains the quality standards, methods and responsibilities used to achieve product quality requirements.

stem: A product passes its checks but has not yet been formally accepted by the named approving authority. What is the correct conclusion?
option_A: The checks alone do not prove formal acceptance
option_B: Acceptance is automatic whenever a test script passes
option_C: Quality control can be skipped because acceptance has not happened
option_D: The project can ignore the acceptance criteria
correct_text: The checks alone do not prove formal acceptance
why: Product checking and authorization for acceptance are related but distinct activities; the defined acceptance authority must act.

stem: Which TWO statements are true? 1. A quality register can record test outcomes. 2. A product register specifies how every stakeholder is communicated with. 3. Quality assurance is normally independent of the project team. 4. A product description is a substitute for the business case.
why: Statement 1 accurately describes recorded quality results, and statement 3 describes assurance independence.

stem: A contractor has not yet confirmed whether crucial equipment will arrive in time. How should the uncertainty be recorded?
option_D: As a completed issue with no uncertainty
why: A risk is an uncertain event or set of events that could affect objectives if it occurs.

stem: Which part of a well-expressed risk explains the existing situation that could lead to an uncertain event?
why: The cause identifies the present source or condition that gives rise to the uncertainty.

stem: A team writes: Due to limited supplier capacity, delivery might slip, increasing overall project cost. Which phrase describes the risk event?
option_D: The project manager reviewing the register
why: The uncertain occurrence is the possible delivery delay between the existing cause and its cost consequences.

stem: A project compares a 20% chance of disruption with a possible one-month delay. What do these numbers describe?
why: The chance is probability, while the projected one-month effect on objectives is impact.

stem: An organization states that it is willing to pursue innovation despite a relatively high level of uncertainty. Which term captures its risk-taking attitude?
why: Risk appetite reflects the amount and type of risk the business is prepared to accept while pursuing objectives.

stem: A project sets the maximum acceptable aggregated risk exposure for a performance objective. Which concept is used?
why: Risk tolerance expresses a measurable limit on acceptable outcomes for an objective at risk.

stem: A register identifies Priya to oversee a threat and Sam to implement an agreed contingency test. Which responsibility is Sam performing?
why: Sam is accountable for completing a specific agreed response action, while Priya oversees the risk.

stem: A potential improvement might arise if a new technology becomes available. The team acts to increase the chance it will occur. Which response applies?
why: Enhancement increases the likelihood or impact of a positive uncertain event.

stem: The risk owner knows the uncertainty and assesses combined exposure before selecting responses. Which risk management technique step is chiefly involved?
why: Assessing estimates probability/impact, prioritizes risks and considers the overall risk profile.

stem: A senior manager dismisses every low-frequency threat because one similar threat did not materialize last year. What should the risk manager challenge?
option_A: Only the project plan version number
why: One reassuring experience can distort judgement; risk management should use evidence rather than unchecked assumptions.

stem: The team needs a documented method for scoring risks, reviewing them and assigning responsibilities. What should it consult?
why: The approach defines the procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities for risk management.

stem: A stakeholder asks to add a new feature to a product whose requirements are approved. What should this be classified as?
why: A proposal to amend an approved product baseline is a request for change and should be handled through issue management.

stem: During inspection, a component is found not to meet its agreed specification. What is the most accurate issue classification?
why: An off-specification means a product will not meet its agreed requirements or specifications.

stem: A product does not meet its full specification, but the competent authority agrees it may be accepted without rework. What is the decision commonly called?
why: A concession accepts a known off-specification without correcting it, subject to suitable authority and control.

stem: The project manager wants the current status of formally managed problems, requests for change and off-specifications. Which product is the best starting point?
why: The issue register maintains status information about issues that need management attention.

stem: A complex issue needs detailed impact assessment, alternatives and a recommended response for decision makers. Which product is most suitable?
why: An issue report documents analysis and a recommended response for a particular issue requiring formal treatment.

stem: Which management product specifies how issues will be captured, assessed, escalated and used to control changes?
why: The approach defines the procedures and responsibilities for issue management and change control.

stem: Who should normally approve a change when the project board has delegated a defined class of decisions to a change authority?
option_A: The team manager regardless of any delegation
option_B: An external stakeholder with no project role
option_C: The project manager in every situation
option_D: The delegated change authority within its limits
correct_text: The delegated change authority within its limits
why: The delegated authority can approve or reject changes within the scope and limits the project board has granted.

stem: A set amount is reserved specifically for approved alterations to baselined products. What is it?
why: The change budget provides authorized funds or constraints for agreed changes to controlled baselines.

stem: A product is approved and placed under change control. What does the term project baseline refer to?
option_A: Only products that have failed quality reviews
option_B: The current approved versions of management and project products subject to change control
option_C: Every draft ever written during the project
correct_text: The current approved versions of management and project products subject to change control
why: The project baseline is the authorized reference against which proposed modifications are assessed.

stem: In the issues technique, the impact of a proposed change on costs, benefits and risk is being evaluated. Which step is being carried out?
why: Assessment examines the effect of an issue across relevant project performance aspects before recommendations and decisions.

stem: A team manager sends the project manager a progress update each Friday. What report is this usually?
why: A checkpoint report provides periodic work package progress information from the team manager to the project manager.

stem: A board member wants an agreed fortnightly status summary without joining the project manager's detailed work-package meetings. Which report should the manager provide?
why: Highlight reports provide the project board with periodic summaries at the agreed reporting frequency.

stem: The board will decide whether to authorize the next stage and needs performance against the stage plan. Which report?
why: An end stage report reviews performance of the completed stage for the board's stage-boundary decision.

stem: A project is closing and the board needs a comparison with the approved project baseline. Which report is appropriate?
why: The end project report evaluates the overall project against its original and updated baselines at closure.

stem: The team identifies a forecast work package tolerance breach. To whom should it first raise an issue?
option_B: Project board directly as an exception report
why: The team manager raises an issue to the project manager for decision on a work package exception.

stem: The project manager forecasts that the management stage will exceed an agreed tolerance despite available corrective action. What should be sent to the board?
option_B: Only the next routine highlight report
option_C: A completed exception plan without authorization
option_D: A new team plan signed only by the team manager
why: A forecast stage exception requires timely escalation via an exception report with analysis and options.

stem: The business layer has authorized a tolerance for the whole project. Who must be consulted if that project-level tolerance is forecast to be breached?
option_A: Senior supplier acting without the board
why: A forecast breach of project-level tolerance exceeds the board's own authority and must be referred to the commissioning business layer.

stem: Which type of control happens because a specific event, such as completion of a management stage, has occurred?
why: Event-driven controls are triggered by milestones, stage boundaries or exception situations rather than a clock.

stem: A project manager records a small informal observation and follow-up action that does not require formal issue control. Which record is appropriate?
why: The daily log provides a flexible place for informal observations, small issues and actions requiring attention.

stem: The team wants to record something learned that could improve this stage and future projects. Which record should be updated?
why: The lessons log captures useful learning as it arises so it can inform later work and projects.

stem: A project wants clarity on how project performance data will be stored, accessed and handled securely. Which approach should it use?
why: This approach defines how digital tools and project data will be managed to support control and reporting.

stem: A project mandate has arrived but the company is unsure whether the idea is worth detailed investigation. Which process establishes whether initiation is worthwhile?
why: Starting up a project gathers enough information to decide whether undertaking initiation is sensible.

stem: Which activity is expected during starting up a project rather than initiating a project?
option_A: Approve the completed project initiation documentation
option_B: Produce a full detailed project plan for all specialist work
option_D: Prepare a plan for the initiation stage
correct_text: Prepare a plan for the initiation stage
why: Start-up sets out the work required to investigate and establish detailed project foundations.

stem: The executive and project manager are identified and lessons from similar efforts reviewed. Which process is being performed?
why: The project management team is initially appointed and previous lessons are considered during start-up.

stem: The project board has received the request to initiate and now decides whether to authorize initiation. Which process contains that board decision?
why: The project board uses directing a project to authorize initiation, the project, stages and closure.

stem: Which process runs from pre-project decisions through final project closure at the directing management level?
why: The board exercises overall control and takes key decisions across the project lifecycle.

stem: Identify the missing words: The [?] process enables the project board to exercise overall control while delegating day-to-day management.
why: Directing a project is the board-level process through which strategic decisions and authorizations are made.

stem: During which process is the detailed business case developed and the project initiation documentation assembled?
why: Initiating a project develops the full justification, approaches and controls used to establish firm project foundations.

stem: The business needs to understand precisely how the project will be managed before committing major resources. Which process has that purpose?
why: Initiating a project establishes enough detail about delivery, governance, controls and justification for informed authorization.

stem: A project manager monitors delivered work packages, authorizes new ones and sends highlight reports to the board. Which process?
why: These activities are central to the project manager's control of an authorized management stage.

stem: The project manager learns that a current-stage issue could require corrective action without breaching stage tolerance. Which process permits day-to-day correction?
why: Within delegated authority, the project manager can take corrective action to maintain an authorized stage.

stem: Which TWO activities are associated with controlling a stage? 1. Authorize work packages. 2. Approve the next stage plan as project board. 3. Review work package status. 4. Confirm final project closure.
why: Authorizing work packages and reviewing their progress are project manager duties within controlling a stage.

stem: The specialist team formally agrees the work it will undertake, creates products and reports progress back. Which process focuses on that agreement?
why: Managing product delivery controls accepting, executing and handing back work agreed in a work package.

stem: Identify the missing words: A team manager uses the [?] process to accept, execute and deliver the work package.
why: The team manager's core delivery interface with the project manager is managing product delivery.

stem: A project manager has prepared the end stage report, updated the business case and drafted the next stage plan. Which process is this?
why: At a stage boundary, information is prepared so the board can review performance and authorize the next stage.

stem: The project board requests an exception plan because the existing stage plan is no longer viable. Which process normally prepares the replacement plan?
why: Managing a stage boundary supports preparation and submission of an exception plan after board direction.

stem: At project completion, the organization needs formal product acceptance, handover and a list of unresolved actions for operations. Which process?
why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, evaluates delivery and ensures follow-on actions are appropriately handed over.

stem: Which TWO statements about closing a project are correct? 1. Some benefit reviews may be planned for after closure. 2. Every expected benefit must already be achieved. 3. Final user acceptance should be checked. 4. Only the team manager may authorize final closure.
why: Post-project benefit reviews can be arranged, and user acceptance must be checked before orderly closure.

stem: Which is NOT an accountability of the senior supplier on the project board?
option_B: Ensuring suitable supplier resources are committed
option_C: Protecting the technical integrity of specialist products
option_D: Owning the business case and the overall investment justification
correct_text: Owning the business case and the overall investment justification
why: Business case ownership belongs to the executive, who represents the business interest.

stem: Which of these is NOT normally a time-driven progress control?
option_A: Exception report issued following a forecast stage tolerance breach
option_D: Scheduled weekly work package progress check
correct_text: Exception report issued following a forecast stage tolerance breach
why: An exception report is triggered by an event: the forecast of exceeding tolerance, not by a regular calendar interval.

stem: Which statement does NOT describe a risk in PRINCE2?
option_A: An uncertain threat with assessed likelihood and impact
option_B: A known off-specification which requires a decision now
option_C: An uncertain event that may increase project costs
option_D: An uncertain event that may improve benefits
correct_text: A known off-specification which requires a decision now
why: An off-specification is an issue because an agreed product requirement is known not to be met.

stem: Which activity is NOT an objective of starting up a project?
option_A: Appoint the initial executive and project manager
option_B: Establish an outline business case and project brief
option_C: Authorize the full delivery project after approving its detailed PID
correct_text: Authorize the full delivery project after approving its detailed PID
why: Full project authorization is a board decision in directing a project after the PID has been developed during initiating a project.

stem: A team asks which integrated PRINCE2 element covers the specific setting in which this project operates. Which one is it?
why: Project context includes organizational and commercial environment, delivery method and other local circumstances.

stem: A team releases a usable part of a product, takes feedback, then improves and extends it in repeated cycles. Which delivery approach is described?
why: The team learns and extends the product across successive increments, which is iterative-incremental delivery.

stem: Two organizations each replace a payroll system. Why can both still be considered unique projects?
option_A: They have distinct contexts, people, requirements or constraints
option_B: Neither can use an established supplier
option_C: Every project must invent a new technology
option_D: The projects cannot use comparable plans
correct_text: They have distinct contexts, people, requirements or constraints
why: Even similar undertakings differ in their circumstances, stakeholders or products; uniqueness does not require novelty in every activity.

stem: A regulator imposes additional data-retention rules on a project midway through delivery. Which part of the project context is most directly relevant?
option_C: The external regulatory and organizational environment
option_D: Whether a project has seven principles
correct_text: The external regulatory and organizational environment
why: Regulatory requirements are contextual constraints to consider when tailoring and maintaining project plans.

stem: A business case was compelling at authorization but costs now exceed the likely benefits. Which principle requires renewed justification?
why: The project must remain worthwhile, not simply have had a good business case at its start.

stem: A manager records an unexpected problem and alters the next stage approach after discussing what the team learned. Which principle is shown?
why: Identifying and applying a lesson during the project demonstrates learning rather than filing lessons only at closure.

stem: A small internal project has one person fulfilling both project support and team manager duties. Which statement best reflects tailoring?
option_A: This can be acceptable if responsibilities are clear and role constraints are respected
option_B: Every PRINCE2 role must be a different person
option_C: The project manager should also provide independent project assurance
option_D: The project may omit the business justification principle
correct_text: This can be acceptable if responsibilities are clear and role constraints are respected
why: Some roles can be combined when suitable, but accountability and independence constraints must remain intact.

stem: The project board approves a stage plan and delegates delivery to the project manager within agreed bounds. Which principle primarily enables this?
why: Tolerances provide boundaries within which lower levels can act without routine escalation.

stem: Which project action most directly demonstrates the focus on products principle?
option_A: Start by listing team members’ favourite activities
option_B: Approve the supplier invoice before stating acceptance criteria
option_C: Define the required product and acceptance criteria before estimating tasks
option_D: Use the same report template for every stage regardless of need
correct_text: Define the required product and acceptance criteria before estimating tasks
why: Starting with the result and its quality expectations keeps the project focused on deliverables.

stem: Which action is consistent with tailoring while retaining PRINCE2?
option_A: Removing the manage by stages principle to save time
option_B: Using a concise combined digital management product with the required information
option_C: Allowing the project manager to act as their own independent assurance
option_D: Omitting approval for a new stage regardless of risk
correct_text: Using a concise combined digital management product with the required information
why: A documented product can be simplified or combined if control, information and accountability needs are satisfied.

stem: The team discovers stakeholder responsibilities are unclear. Which principle most clearly addresses this?
why: The principle requires defined accountabilities and effective relationships across the stakeholder interests.

stem: A project uses an iterative delivery method but retains board authorizations and clear tolerances. What is this an example of?
option_B: Replacing PRINCE2 with a software development methodology
option_C: Removing the directing a project process
option_D: Removing the focus on products principle
why: The method can support different delivery approaches while retaining principles and accountability.

stem: Identify the missing words. A PRINCE2 project is planned, monitored and controlled on a ______ basis.
why: Manage by stages gives the board controlled review and commitment points during the project.

stem:
Which two actions demonstrate learning from experience?
1. Seek relevant lessons before initiation.
2. Wait until closure to record any lessons.
3. Update the next stage’s approach based on lessons learned.
4. Use only lessons from this project, never external ones.
why: Both early use of lessons and applying lessons to later stages demonstrate continuous learning.

stem: A system is delivered, but staff affected by it have not been trained and refuse to adopt it. What does this mainly illustrate?
option_A: The project should measure only product delivery
option_B: People affected by a project matter as well as those delivering it
option_C: Every affected person needs a seat on the project board
option_D: All benefits are guaranteed by product acceptance
correct_text: People affected by a project matter as well as those delivering it
why: Managing change requires attention to the people who must work differently after handover.

stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes leadership from management in a project?
option_A: Leadership is budget control; management is motivating change
option_B: Management is unnecessary if leadership is strong
option_C: Leadership influences direction and commitment; management coordinates work and controls
option_D: Leadership belongs only to the project executive
correct_text: Leadership influences direction and commitment; management coordinates work and controls
why: Leadership builds commitment to change while management plans, organizes and monitors delivery.

stem: A project has a formal stakeholder list but no two-way conversations with affected teams. What is missing?
why: Engagement involves listening and shaping the change, not just storing stakeholder names.

stem: A charity project must send board updates by email, staff demos in person, and patient surveys online. Which PID approach specifies this mix of communication and feedback?
why: It describes communication needs, channels, responsibilities, frequencies and feedback arrangements.

stem: A department must adopt new working practices after a product is delivered. Where should planned activities to support this transition be described?
why: This explains how changes to working practices and their adoption by affected people will be managed.

stem: A team includes multiple languages and working cultures. Which capability most directly helps leaders collaborate effectively across these differences?
option_C: An extra management stage in every case
option_D: Removing remote workers from the team
why: Understanding and working respectfully across cultural contexts supports effective diverse teams.

stem: A team member can perform a task but does not have enough available hours for it. Which distinction matters?
why: Capability concerns ability; capacity concerns available resources or time to do the work.

stem: A distributed team argues about handover standards and deadlines. Which action best supports effective collaboration?
option_A: Keep team members apart and avoid discussing differences
option_B: Agree working practices, communication norms and interfaces together
option_C: Escalate every disagreement to the business layer
correct_text: Agree working practices, communication norms and interfaces together
why: Shared, explicit working practices and co-creation improve trust and coordination across locations.

stem: A senior stakeholder announces a change without explaining why it matters to staff. Which leadership improvement is most relevant?
option_A: Increase the number of checkpoint reports
option_B: Replace the issue register with a spreadsheet
option_C: Explain the vision and involve affected people in the change
option_D: Ask project assurance to approve every team conversation
correct_text: Explain the vision and involve affected people in the change
why: Leadership helps people understand and support a future state rather than merely receive instructions.

stem: Why is the change management approach relevant even when specialist products are technically complete?
option_A: It eliminates the need for user acceptance
option_B: It ensures all financial benefits arise instantly
option_D: It supports adoption of the new state and achievement of outcomes
correct_text: It supports adoption of the new state and achievement of outcomes
why: Delivered outputs create value only if people and operations use them to achieve intended change.

stem:
Which two practices make communication with stakeholders effective?
1. Match channels and frequency to stakeholder needs.
2. Send every stakeholder exactly the same technical detail.
3. Seek feedback and respond to it.
