4. Restrict engagement to members of the project management team.
why: Both appropriate communication design and two-way feedback support engagement and collaboration.

stem: Who may need to be engaged when project products change operational job roles?
option_C: Only the team members building the product
option_D: People working on the project and those affected by its change
correct_text: People working on the project and those affected by its change
why: PRINCE2’s people element covers both the project ecosystem and stakeholders impacted by its outcomes.

stem: A team member has technical expertise but repeatedly ignores agreed working practices. Which is the most complete way to view team effectiveness?
option_A: Consider skills, behaviours, relationships and working culture together
option_C: Ignore relationships as outside the project
option_D: Replace all team collaboration with formal reports
correct_text: Consider skills, behaviours, relationships and working culture together
why: Team effectiveness depends on more than specialist skill, including collaboration and the ability to work together.

stem: A user group is influential but skeptical about a proposed new process. What is the best initial response?
option_A: Understand their concerns and involve them in shaping the change
option_B: Treat skepticism as proof of an exception situation
option_C: Ignore them because they are not on the project board
option_D: Record the group only in the risk register and stop communicating
correct_text: Understand their concerns and involve them in shaping the change
why: Engagement should be two-way and responsive to affected people’s motivations and needs.

stem: Identify the missing word. The ______ management approach in the PID describes how feedback is gathered and information shared with stakeholders.
why: The communication management approach defines who needs information, how it will be communicated and when.

stem:
Project staff understand what to build but do not know how the organization will change after delivery. Which two actions help most?
1. Describe the current and target operating states.
2. Treat organizational adoption as outside project concerns.
3. Plan transition and communication with affected users.
4. Measure project success only by completion of technical work.
why: A clear desired future state and planned transition/engagement help people make the change.

stem: A team has specialists with strong individual skills but poor cooperation. What is the most likely gap?
option_B: Team cohesion and effective working relationships
correct_text: Team cohesion and effective working relationships
why: Individual skills alone do not create trust, shared goals or coordinated delivery.

stem: A new booking system is delivered to a hospital. Patients then book appointments online. Which is the outcome?
option_C: A measured reduction of 20 minutes per call
why: An outcome is the change in real-world behaviour following use of the delivered outputs.

stem: A project replaces travel with video meetings, reducing costs but also reducing local café revenue. What is the café revenue reduction from the investing organization’s perspective if recognized as an expected negative effect?
why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization.

stem: A project is likely to finish on time but planned operational savings may only arrive two years later. Which approach identifies how the savings will be reviewed after closure?
why: This defines benefit reviews, responsible parties and management actions for realizing benefits, including post-project reviews.

stem: Which PID approach defines how sustainability targets will be reviewed and controlled?
why: It identifies actions, reviews and controls to meet agreed sustainability performance targets.

stem: At a stage boundary the business case is updated using actual expenditure and revised benefits. What is the main reason?
option_A: To support a fresh decision on continued investment
option_B: To prove all forecast benefits have already been realized
option_D: To authorize the team manager to approve the entire project
correct_text: To support a fresh decision on continued investment
why: The board needs current cost, risk and benefit forecasts rather than relying solely on assumptions made at initiation.

stem: Identify the missing word. In the business case technique, ______ means keeping the business case current with actual and forecast information.
why: Maintain keeps the business case updated as the project progresses and information changes.

stem: Which activity is closest to the CHECK step of business case management?
option_D: Assess whether remaining cost and risk are justified by expected value
correct_text: Assess whether remaining cost and risk are justified by expected value
why: Checking the business case tests whether further investment remains desirable, viable and achievable.

stem: A project product will be delivered successfully, but the proposed outcome no longer supports the organization’s strategy. What should be revisited?
option_C: Business case alignment with business objectives
option_D: Only the team members’ work instructions
correct_text: Business case alignment with business objectives
why: Investment needs to remain justified by expected benefits and their contribution to business objectives.

stem:
Which two statements about outputs, outcomes and benefits are CORRECT?
1. A specialist deliverable can be an output.
2. Every output automatically guarantees a benefit.
3. Changed operational behaviour can be an outcome.
4. Benefits can never be measured after closure.
why: Outputs are what gets delivered; outcomes are changes that arise when outputs are used.

stem: During pre-project work, a small amount of justification is assembled before full initiation. Which management product best captures this initial rationale and scope?
why: The project brief gives a common starting point and can include the outline business case before detailed initiation.

stem: A project’s senior user requests a feature while the senior supplier worries about technical feasibility. What are these roles representing?
option_B: User need and supplier delivery capability respectively
option_C: The board and the project manager respectively
option_D: Quality assurance and project assurance respectively
correct_text: User need and supplier delivery capability respectively
why: Senior users represent requirements and benefits; senior suppliers represent resources and technical feasibility.

stem: The project needs to define contracts, procurement relationships and how suppliers will be managed commercially. Which PID product is most relevant?
why: This records how commercial relationships, agreements and supplier arrangements are managed.

stem: A product depends on two specialist teams. Which organizing aid best breaks the delivery work into manageable work elements?
why: A work breakdown structure decomposes the work needed to deliver products and helps organize responsibilities.

stem: Which role remains ultimately accountable for the project’s business case and success?
why: The executive is the single point of accountability and owns the project’s business justification.

stem: A supplier cannot provide the specialist test staff promised for the project. Which project board role should address supplier capacity?
why: The senior supplier is responsible for representing and securing supplier resources and technical capability.

stem: A project manager has sufficient specialist knowledge and wants to manage a small team directly. Which role may they also undertake?
why: The project manager can perform team-manager responsibilities where scale, skills and capacity make this suitable.

stem: Which PID product makes clear who has authority and responsibilities in the project management team?
option_D: Project management team structure and role descriptions
correct_text: Project management team structure and role descriptions
why: The structure and role descriptions show the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships.

stem: The project board has delegated authority to approve certain changes to a named person. Which role has been established?
why: A change authority decides specified requests within limits delegated by the project board.

stem: Which step is most relevant when a project reviews who its affected external parties are before designing governance?
why: The organizing technique begins by considering the relevant business, user, supplier and wider relationships.

stem: The project board wants independent checks but asks the project manager to provide their own assurance. Why is this inappropriate?
option_A: The project manager is too busy to write reports
option_B: All assurance must be done by an external certification body
option_C: Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager
option_D: Assurance is only needed after closure
correct_text: Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager
why: The board retains accountability for assurance and must maintain an independent line of review.

stem: A plan shows that testing cannot start until configuration is complete. What planning concept is described?
why: A dependency is a relationship in which one work item or product relies on another.

stem: Which management product formally tells a delivery team which products to create and the applicable constraints?
why: It describes the delegated delivery, products, constraints, reporting and acceptance requirements.

stem: A project is planned in detail for the next stage but only in outline for much later stages. Which concept supports this?
why: Planning detail should reflect the available certainty; near work can be planned more precisely.

stem: Which statement distinguishes a project plan from a stage plan?
option_A: The project plan gives the high-level overall picture; a stage plan gives detailed control for one stage
option_B: A stage plan replaces the project plan for the whole project
option_C: Only the team manager uses a project plan
option_D: A project plan is always produced after the final stage
correct_text: The project plan gives the high-level overall picture; a stage plan gives detailed control for one stage
why: The plans serve different management levels and planning horizons.

stem: An approved stage plan can no longer deliver within tolerance. The board asks for a replacement plan. What type is prepared?
why: An approved exception plan replaces the stage or project plan for the period it covers.

stem: A project manager starts planning by defining deliverables before listing activities. Which technique does this illustrate?
why: Defining and analysing products first is central to PRINCE2 planning.

stem: In the PRINCE2 planning technique, which activity should follow defining and analysing products?
why: The planning technique organizes the work packages after clarifying the required products.

stem: Which product primarily defines the full project’s acceptance criteria, rather than one component’s quality checks?
why: This defines what the whole project must deliver, including user quality expectations and acceptance criteria.

stem: A team manager wants to coordinate detailed specialist work within an agreed work package. Which plan is most directly useful, if required?
why: A team plan can organize and control a delivery team’s work under an agreed work package.

stem:
Which two statements about management stages are correct?
1. They establish control and investment decision points.
2. They must always end at the same time as technical phases.
3. The initiation stage is a management stage.
4. Management stages should overlap to save time.
why: Management stages create decision points, and initiation is the first management stage.

stem: A product must process 500 payments per minute during acceptance testing. What type of information is that?
why: A measurable throughput threshold defines a specific characteristic to be verified during quality control.

stem: A test was completed and a product failed against its defined criteria. Which record should reflect the test result?
why: The quality register tracks planned and completed quality activities and their results, including failures.

stem: A project manager wants a current list of project products and their status. Which management product is most directly relevant?
why: The product register records the products being managed and their status.

stem: A user says a new application must be easy to navigate. Which further step makes the expectation useful for quality control?
option_A: Assume any screen layout is acceptable
option_B: Record it only as a financial risk
option_C: Delay defining any quality checks until closure
option_D: Agree observable, measurable quality specifications and methods
correct_text: Agree observable, measurable quality specifications and methods
why: Clear specifications and tests enable the team to check whether the expectation is met.

stem: What BEST distinguishes quality assurance from product quality control?
option_A: Assurance always tests every finished product, while control audits the organization
option_B: Assurance checks confidence in the quality system; control tests products against specifications
option_C: They are two names for the same activity
option_D: Control only starts once the project closes
correct_text: Assurance checks confidence in the quality system; control tests products against specifications
why: Quality assurance is often independently managed, while quality control checks product conformity.

stem: Which management product explains the standards, quality methods and roles to use throughout the project?
why: This defines methods, standards and responsibilities for quality specifications and acceptance criteria.

stem: A supplier has completed technical testing but the user has not agreed the product meets operational needs. What should the project avoid assuming?
option_A: That passing technical tests automatically proves user acceptance
option_B: That quality testing needs recorded evidence
option_D: That quality management runs throughout delivery
correct_text: That passing technical tests automatically proves user acceptance
why: Technical conformance is not the same as satisfying the user’s agreed acceptance criteria.

stem: Which part of quality management starts by defining what the product must meet and how that will be checked?
why: Quality planning captures specifications and develops product descriptions and the quality approach.

stem:
Which two statements about a Product Description are correct?
1. It includes quality criteria for that product.
2. It replaces the project-wide business case.
3. It can specify the quality method to use.
4. It is always the record of completed quality test results.
why: A Product Description states the product’s quality criteria and how those criteria are to be checked.

stem: A project is creating many similar outputs. Which practice helps ensure each product is checked using agreed standards before acceptance?
why: The quality practice defines and applies methods to establish whether products satisfy agreed specifications.

stem: A contractor may miss a delivery date because its factory is at risk of flooding. Which phrase describes the risk cause?
option_D: An exception report to the board
why: The underlying situation creates the possibility of a later risk event.

stem: For a threat, which description best captures risk impact?
option_A: How likely the event is to occur
option_B: How near the event is in time
option_C: How rapidly consequences develop after it occurs
option_D: The estimated effect on project objectives if it occurs
correct_text: The estimated effect on project objectives if it occurs
why: Impact is the magnitude and nature of consequences for project objectives.

stem: A manager estimates the probability of a cyberattack, then considers all identified threats together. Which activity is most relevant to the combined picture?
option_C: Assessing overall risk exposure or the risk profile
correct_text: Assessing overall risk exposure or the risk profile
why: Aggregate analysis helps understand the combined effect of risks rather than one risk alone.

stem: A potential threat is eliminated by selecting a different supplier that has no exposure to the relevant hazard. Which threat response is this?
why: Avoid removes the threat by changing the circumstances that created it or removing the exposure.

stem: A favourable uncertainty could be made more likely by funding a small prototype. Which opportunity response is described?
why: Enhance takes action to improve the probability or impact of a potential opportunity.

stem: Who is responsible for ensuring that an assigned risk is managed and appropriate responses are monitored?
why: The risk owner is accountable for the assigned risk and for coordinating/monitoring responses.

stem: A team notices it is choosing optimistic estimates because it wants the project approved. What should the team address?
why: Recognizing and challenging optimism bias improves the quality of risk assessments and decisions.

stem: Identify the missing word. The PRINCE2 risk technique includes identify, assess, plan, implement and ______.
why: Risk information needs to be communicated throughout the risk management technique to relevant parties.

stem: A project has a high appetite for taking an opportunity, but a defined tolerance threshold for its risk exposure. What is the distinction?
option_A: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is a measurable allowed limit
option_B: Appetite is a cash reserve; tolerance is a supplier invoice
option_C: Both always describe the same money amount
option_D: Tolerance tells when a risk might occur
correct_text: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is a measurable allowed limit
why: Appetite expresses attitude to risk; tolerance sets a measurable boundary for acceptable exposure or performance.

stem: A planned response would lower the financial effect of a threat if it occurs by purchasing insurance. What response does this most closely represent?
why: An insurance agreement transfers specified financial consequences of a threat to another party.

stem: A completed product is found to be below its approved specification. Which type of issue is most relevant?
why: A product that will not meet its agreed specification is an off-specification issue.

stem: An employee proposes adding a new report to a signed-off product. What is this proposal?
why: A proposal to alter an already approved baseline is a request for change.

stem: What should the team check FIRST when assessing a change proposal that may affect scope and benefits?
option_A: Its effect on the business case, baseline and related objectives
option_B: Whether an invoice has already been issued
option_C: How to hide the request from stakeholders
option_D: Whether all requested changes must automatically be accepted
correct_text: Its effect on the business case, baseline and related objectives
why: Assessment should consider impacts on project justification, products, time, cost and risks before approval.

stem: Which step of the issues technique makes a reasoned comparison of possible responses before an approval decision?
why: The recommend step evaluates possible options and proposes an appropriate response to the decision-maker.

stem: A change has been approved and the controlled product record must be updated. Which step of issue management is this?
why: Implementation carries out the approved action and updates affected baselines and records.

stem: Which management product provides detailed analysis and recommendations for an issue requiring formal handling?
why: An issue report can document description, impact assessment, options and recommendations for a significant issue.

stem: A project board delegates approval of small requests for change but retains expensive decisions. What is being tailored?
option_A: The levels of change authority and delegated limits
option_B: The existence of the business justification principle
option_C: The requirement to log formal issues
option_D: The need to consider product baselines
correct_text: The levels of change authority and delegated limits
why: Decision rights may be delegated proportionately, with larger impacts reserved for the board.

stem: What is the key risk of delegating change approvals too widely without suitable controls?
option_A: Every request will have to go to the project board
option_B: Decisions may drift away from the overall business justification
option_C: All changes become future risks instead of issues
option_D: Product descriptions can no longer be created
correct_text: Decisions may drift away from the overall business justification
why: Fragmented approvals can weaken alignment between individual changes and the project business case.

stem: The team needs project-wide guidance on how requests for change will be captured, assessed, decided and implemented. Where is this found?
why: This defines issue resolution and change-control procedures, responsibilities and delegated authority.

stem:
Which two statements about issues are correct?
1. An issue can be a concern requiring assessment.
2. Every issue is necessarily a request for change.
3. An unexpected business opportunity may be recorded as an issue.
4. Issues only exist after project closure.
why: Issues include concerns and business opportunities that require project management consideration.

stem: At a fixed weekly interval, a team manager informs the project manager about work-package delivery. Which report is used?
why: A checkpoint report is the agreed regular team-to-project-manager progress report for a work package.

stem: The project manager needs to summarize stage progress at agreed intervals for the project board. Which report is most appropriate?
why: The project manager uses highlight reports to keep the board informed on stage progress at regular intervals.

stem: The forecast finish date breaches the stage time tolerance even though the date has not yet arrived. How should this be treated?
option_A: Wait until the actual late finish before reporting
option_B: Ask the team to ignore the agreed tolerance
option_C: Change the approved stage baseline without authority
option_D: Escalate the forecast stage exception to the project board
correct_text: Escalate the forecast stage exception to the project board
why: A forecast outside stage tolerance requires the project manager to raise an exception report.

stem: Which control is event-driven rather than time-driven?
option_A: The board authorization of the next stage
correct_text: The board authorization of the next stage
why: Stage-end authorization occurs at a defined event, not an agreed regular time interval.

stem: A team manager predicts a work package will breach tolerance. What should the team manager do initially?
option_A: Send an exception report directly to the project board
option_B: Raise an issue with the project manager
option_D: Wait for a formal end project report
correct_text: Raise an issue with the project manager
why: The team manager refers a forecast work-package breach to the project manager for a decision.

stem: What does the end project report primarily enable?
option_A: Routine delegation of a new work package
option_B: The project manager’s weekly status communication
option_C: Evaluation of completed project performance against agreed baselines
option_D: Automatic confirmation of all benefits scheduled after closure
correct_text: Evaluation of completed project performance against agreed baselines
why: The end project report supports closure with a view of achievement, variances, benefits and lessons.

stem: Which product is best for recording an informal day-to-day matter that the project manager can handle without formal escalation?
why: The daily log can capture informal issues, reminders and other day-to-day matters.

stem: A project needs an agreed plan for how project information is captured, stored, protected and used in reporting. Which PID approach is most relevant?
why: This approach sets how digital information and data will be managed for reliable project control.

stem: What is the difference between a forecast and a tolerance?
option_A: A forecast is an approved baseline; tolerance is the daily log
option_B: A forecast predicts an outcome; tolerance defines the permitted deviation
option_C: Both are names for a stage plan
option_D: Tolerance predicts the completion date; forecast grants authority
correct_text: A forecast predicts an outcome; tolerance defines the permitted deviation
why: Comparing forecasts with tolerances allows managers to detect possible exceptions early.

stem:
Which two reports are normally time-driven?
1. Checkpoint report.
2. Exception report.
3. Highlight report.
4. End stage report.
why: Checkpoint and highlight reports are typically produced at agreed intervals.

stem: A business asks whether a proposed project is worth investigating, before funding detailed initiation. Which process supports this decision?
why: Starting up prepares the outline case and brief to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.

stem: Which process gives the project board authority to authorize initiation, delivery stages and closure?
why: The board’s process makes major authorization and direction decisions throughout the lifecycle.

stem: What is the central result of initiating a project before substantial delivery investment?
option_A: A guaranteed complete benefit realization report
option_C: Only a list of potential suppliers
option_D: A credible set of foundations and project initiation documentation
correct_text: A credible set of foundations and project initiation documentation
why: Initiation develops enough business, plan, quality and control information for the board to decide on delivery.

stem: A project manager authorizes a work package and monitors the stage’s progress. Which process is being used?
why: The project manager delegates, monitors and takes corrective action during a stage.

stem: A team manager agrees a work package with the project manager, executes it and returns completed products. Which process describes this?
why: Team managers use this process to accept, execute and deliver agreed product work.

stem: Near the end of a stage, the project manager updates the overall plan and prepares a detailed next-stage plan. Which process is being used?
why: This process prepares the next stage plan and updated evidence for board decisions.

stem: The final product has been accepted. The project manager evaluates performance and asks the board to authorize closure. Which process is central?
why: The process confirms acceptance, handover, evaluation and orderly closure or premature closure.

stem: Which process operates across the entire project, even as the project manager moves through several stages?
why: The project board’s directing process spans authorization, stage decisions and closure across the project lifecycle.

stem: During starting up a project, what is normally prepared to plan the work needed for the next process?
option_D: Team plan for every specialist group
why: The initiation stage plan sets the work and resources needed to create the PID and other initiation products.

stem: After starting up, the project manager asks for permission to enter initiation. Which process handles the board’s authorization?
why: The project board authorizes initiation through its directing process.

stem: A completed work package has been returned by a team manager. In which process will the project manager normally review it for stage progress?
why: The project manager reviews completed work and monitors stage progress in controlling a stage.

stem: An exception report has been considered and the board requests a replacement stage plan. Where is that replacement developed?
why: An exception plan can be prepared under managing a stage boundary when directed by the board.

stem: Identify the missing words. The purpose of ______ is to control the link between the project manager and team manager for specialist products.
why: This process agrees requirements for accepting, executing, reporting and delivering work-package products.

stem: A project is being terminated early because its remaining costs cannot be justified. Which statement best describes proper management?
option_A: Abandon all remaining records and transfer staff immediately
option_B: Use closing a project to perform an orderly premature close
option_C: Continue spending until the original final date regardless of value
option_D: Authorize new delivery work packages without reviewing the decision
correct_text: Use closing a project to perform an orderly premature close
why: PRINCE2’s closure process supports both normal and premature closure with appropriate review and handover.

stem:
Which two process statements are correct?
1. Directing a project provides board-level control.
2. Starting up a project creates the detailed PID.
3. Initiating a project prepares the project’s detailed foundations.
4. Managing product delivery authorizes all management stages.
why: Directing makes key board decisions; initiating establishes the detailed case, plan and controls.

stem: Which process confirms that acceptance of the overall project product is formally recognized?
why: Closing provides the fixed point for confirmation of overall project product acceptance.

stem: A project has two technical workstreams proceeding concurrently. What does PRINCE2 require of management stages?
option_A: The two management stages must overlap exactly like the technical workstreams
option_B: Management stages form sequential governance periods, even if technical work overlaps
option_C: There can be no more than one management stage
option_D: Each technical skill must have its own separate management stage
correct_text: Management stages form sequential governance periods, even if technical work overlaps
why: Technical teams may work concurrently while board control is structured by management stage boundaries.

stem:
The project board requests an updated overall viability assessment at the end of a stage. Which two outputs are most relevant?
1. End stage report.
2. Next stage plan.
3. Team members’ personal calendars only.
4. Unapproved supplier change requests only.
why: The end stage report and next stage plan help the board judge past progress and the next commitment.

stem: A project manager must send a completed PID to the board for a delivery authorization decision. Which process has just provided that information?
why: Initiation assembles the PID for the project board’s later authorization decision under directing a project.
